     1	# Roles, communication and state
     2	
     3	## Program orchestrator — thin scheduler and landing coordinator
     4	
     5	Owns the DAG, sequencing, dependencies, capacity and landing order. Spawns and steers block
     6	orchestrators and the landing agent — nothing else — and is the single landing authority.
     7	
     8	Never implements, runs a review-fix cycle, manages implementers or reviewers, or ingests raw worker
     9	logs, traces or review reports — it reads compact receipts only. Reacts to milestone, blocker,
    10	decision and completion events rather than polling. Keeps only unblocked trains active; checkpoints
    11	or shuts down finished teammates.
    12	
    13	## Block orchestrator — owns durable local context
    14	
    15	Owns the charter, scope boundary, relevant architecture, dependencies, settled decisions, acceptance
    16	criteria, and decomposition into reviewable slices.
    17	
    18	Spawns one manager and resumes it while it remains effective, priming it with the relevant
    19	architecture and current slice — not the whole doctrine. Validates scope and completion without
    20	duplicating code review. Sends compact events upward. Never implements.
    21	
    22	**A block drives itself to ready. Everything inside its charter is its decision, including the
    23	authority instruments its own work needs.** It determines which instrument is required, authors it,
    24	obtains its ratification by consult — that verdict is the decision, not advice — performs the
    25	ratifying acts its own scope covers, and dispositions its own findings. It does not ask permission to
    26	proceed with work it owns.
    27	
    28	Instruments and evidence accumulate on the block's own line. **The program orchestrator places and
    29	registers them once, from the ready package, at landing** — not one at a time, mid-flight. A block
    30	that escalates each instrument as it is produced converts its own authority into a queue.
    31	
    32	**Escalate only four things:** a conflict with another block, a change to program structure or a
    33	dependency edge, an act on an artifact another block owns, or a consult returning inconclusive after
    34	one attempt. Everything else is the block's, and a question that could be settled by reading the
    35	charter or the tree is not an escalation.
    36	
    37	**A block owner gets its own rulings.** Design, wording, in-charter scope and evidence questions go
    38	to an architecture consult (`prompts/architect.md`) — read-only, question-shaped and unprimed, asking
    39	whether something violates a named invariant rather than asking for confirmation. That verdict is the
    40	recorded decision. Escalate to the program orchestrator only for landing order and the machine,
    41	ledger and authority-registry writes, cross-block conflicts, a charter scope change, or a consult
    42	that comes back inconclusive. Where the option set collapses to one survivor under a rule and a
    43	proven fact, decide and record it — a consult that cannot change the answer buys a record, not a
    44	decision.
    45	
    46	**Its role ends at reporting the block ready and verified** — the candidate identity, the evidence,
    47	and the manager's drafted squash message. That report is an input to landing confirmation, never a
    48	substitute for it: the program orchestrator, or the landing agent acting for it, confirms
    49	independently.
    50	
    51	**A block never authorises itself.** A block branch carries no authority-registry delta — the registry
    52	is authored trunk-side by its owner and inherited byte-for-byte through rebase, so a branch-local
    53	registry edit is dropped rather than repaired. The ledger's `base_sha` and everything under
    54	`repository.*` are orchestrator-owned in the same way.
    55	
    56	## Manager — owns delivery
    57	
    58	Dispatches implementation, selects risk-appropriate review lanes, adjudicates and deduplicates
    59	findings, verifies a potentially blocking finding before it interrupts an implementer, dispatches the
    60	smallest sufficient fix, and manages targeted re-review and acceptance. Drafts the squash message —
    61	subject and body — at verification, and sends it upward with the acceptance evidence.
    62	
    63	Stops when acceptance is met and no confirmed in-scope blocker remains. Escalates architecture, scope
    64	or non-convergence rather than buying more rounds. Never writes production code.
    65	
    66	## Workers
    67	
    68	Implementers write code and its tests. Reviewers are independent and read-only. External tool
    69	sessions (Codex, Grok) are manager-controlled workers, not teammates. Claude workers run in-process
    70	or in the supplied CLI pool (runtime modes, `README.md`); the role contract is identical in both.
    71	
    72	**One writer per candidate worktree at a time.** Parallel implementers only for naturally independent
    73	slices with disjoint ownership, isolated worktrees and stable boundaries.
    74	
    75	## Communication contract
    76	
    77	**Program → block:** objective; in-scope and out-of-scope boundaries; acceptance criteria; relevant
    78	architecture paths; dependencies; available capacity; any binding user instruction.
    79	
    80	**Block → program:**
    81	
    82	    STATUS: running | blocked | ready | complete
    83	    RESULT: <one sentence>
    84	    CANDIDATE_SHA: <the sha the evidence binds to, or none>
    85	    EVIDENCE: <paths or commands>
    86	    SQUASH_MESSAGE: <subject and body — required on ready>
    87	    ACCEPTANCE_COVERAGE: <each material change → the acceptance id covering it — required on ready>
    88	    DECISION_NEEDED: <only if blocked>
    89	    NEXT: <next material action>
    90	
    91	**Manager → block:** outcome; changed scope if any; acceptance evidence; the drafted squash message;
    92	confirmed unresolved risks; required decision if any.
    93	
    94	**An idle notification is not completion.** A role sends its result before going idle.
    95	
    96	Do not repeatedly paste SHAs, digests, diffs or reports between layers. Raw logs and review traces
    97	stay out of parent contexts and are referenced by path.
    98	
    99	## Block state — one compact record, replaced in place
   100	
   101	Not an append-only ledger. One file per active block, containing only:
   102	
   103	    OBJECTIVE:      what this block delivers
   104	    IN SCOPE:       what it may change
   105	    OUT OF SCOPE:   what it may not
   106	    ARCHITECTURE:   the invariants and paths that bind it
   107	    ACCEPTANCE:     the criteria, each with how it will be evidenced
   108	    SLICE:          the current review slice
   109	    CANDIDATE_SHA:  the frozen candidate under review, or empty
   110	    DECIDED:        settled decisions, with what settled them
   111	    DONE:           completed work
   112	    OPEN:           confirmed findings still open
   113	    BLOCKED ON:     required decisions, or empty
   114	    EVIDENCE:       latest validation, by path
   115	    NEXT:           next material action
   116	
   117	Agents reread it after a resume or context replacement. If an agent repeats mistakes, contradicts
   118	settled decisions, forgets scope or degrades, checkpoint and replace it — reuse is the default, not a
   119	law.
   120	
   121	## Large blocks
   122	
   123	Large cohesive blocks are legitimate. Do not force decomposition on line, commit or file count alone;
   124	treat size as a signal. Decompose for independent acceptance boundaries, owners, risks or review
   125	surfaces.
   126	
   127	Keep one persistent block orchestrator. Give each slice explicit scope and acceptance evidence, and
   128	review it while its context is small — the acceptance phase in `review.md` is what covers cross-slice
   129	behaviour, so do not rerun a cumulative review after every slice. Targeted tests per slice; the full
   130	gate only on the final landing candidate. Do not invent interfaces or scaffolding to make artificial
   131	slices. Sequential slices when ownership overlaps; parallel only for genuinely independent work.
   132	
   133	A block that does not converge after targeted fix cycles is resliced or escalated, not reviewed
   134	harder.
   135	
   136	## Liveness
   137	
   138	**A worker stops when it reports and stays stopped.** That is correct for finished work and a defect
   139	for unfinished work, and nothing notices the difference on its own. Twice in one session a block sat
   140	idle with work owed, surfaced only because someone happened to ask.
   141	
   142	**Keep a roster, not a memory.** Every block is non-complete (live, or parked with the unblocking
   143	EVENT named so the check is on the event rather than the agent), or complete (stopping is correct;
   144	do not resume). Sweep it on a cadence: compare the roster against what is actually running, resume
   145	anything non-complete that stopped, and check whether a parked block's event has fired.
   146	
   147	**A worker stamps its stop reason** — reported-and-complete, reported-and-owed, waiting on an
   148	external run, blocked on a decision. Without it a sweep sees stop-to-resume time and cannot tell idle
   149	from working, so the cost of a cadence is unmeasurable.
   150	
   151	**Sweep cadence is the cheapest lever and the first one to take.** Expected idle per stop is half the
   152	interval; shortening it cuts idle proportionally at no coordination cost. Take that before adding a
   153	seat.
   154	
   155	**Add a second orchestrator seat only above roughly five non-complete blocks, or when blocks need
   156	real-time adjudication rather than resumption** — below that a sweep services them and the cost is
   157	idle minutes. Two seats double the surface for divergent judgement without doubling the checking, and
   158	this program's expensive failures have been judgement, not throughput. If block count forces it: block
   159	ownership is disjoint in the roster so no block is addressable twice; one decision authority per
   160	question class, or two seats rule differently on the same doctrine and both cite it; the roster is the
   161	only coordination artifact, never seat-to-seat messages about state; and escalation precedence is
   162	defined, so a trigger neither arrives twice nor is assumed sent by the other seat.
   163	
   164	**A standing check that depends on the checker surviving is not standing.** Write the roster to disk,
   165	where it outlives the session that maintains it; a schedule is ephemeral and the file is not. The
   166	successor's first act is to read it.
   167	
   168	## Machine resources
   169	
   170	Read-only review work may run in parallel. Write work runs only in isolated ownership.
   171	
   172	**Heavy Cargo work — a full gate, a build, a mutation run — goes through the machine semaphore:**
   173	
   174	    rust-lock.sh <name> -- <command>
   175	
   176	Host-provided, on `PATH`; verify `command -v rust-lock.sh` before the first dispatch that needs it.
   177	It bounds concurrent builds host-wide — not memory — and passes through re-entrantly, so a nested call
   178	cannot deadlock on a slot its own tree holds. A "wait until no cargo is running, then start" check is
   179	not mutual exclusion — every waiter sees idle at once and they all start together.
   180	
   181	A gate carries its own memory ceiling and aborts its child tree on breach; a bare `cargo nextest`
   182	under the semaphore carries none, so shed that unprotected workload first. Steer on swap used, not
   183	free RAM — macOS keeps free pages near zero by design, and `vm_stat` reports its own page size, which
   184	is not 4096 on Apple Silicon. Take two `loadavg` samples before calling a trend.
   185	
   186	Cargo waiting on a target lock is not progress; do not read it as a stalled agent. Run the full gate
   187	only on the final landing candidate; workers run targeted affected checks.

    13	need. Future extensibility is case-by-case, never a default.

   217	## Instruments that observe absence
   218	
   219	An absence fixture — a compile-fail test, a DELETE roster, a "this path no longer exists" assertion —
   220	fails in a direction ordinary tests do not: **it reports success when it has gone blind.** A test that
   221	asserts presence goes red when it can no longer see. A test that asserts absence goes green.
   222	
   223	**An absence fixture must live somewhere that retains the ability to name the surface it denies.** A

   225	them. When that edge was deleted, every error became `E0433` with the caret on the crate segment — the
   226	fixture could no longer name the crate at all, and **would have failed identically if every forbidden
   227	path still existed.** Five of eight lines permanently unobservable, reporting success throughout.
   228	
   229	**A transition that deletes a dependency edge blinds every absence fixture that looked across it.**
   230	Witness and witnessed are coupled through the very edge the work removes, so the transition
   231	necessarily blinds its own instrument. This is a structural property of deletion work, not an
   232	oversight: any block whose job is removing an edge inherits it, and should enumerate the affected
   233	fixtures before moving anything rather than discovering one at a time.
   234	
   235	**Control an absence fixture in both directions.** Re-introduce a deleted path: the expectation must
   236	stop matching and the test must fail. Remove it again: it must pass. A fixture that passes both ways
   237	is hollow, and blindness and success are otherwise the same observation. This is the revert control
   238	inverted, and it is mandatory on deletion work rather than advisory.
   239	
   240	**Assert the error code and its location, never merely that compilation failed.** A fixture that
   241	accepts any compile error accepts its own blindness. `E0433` on a crate segment and `E0432`/`E0603` on

   304	holds is routinely filed as evidence that the instrument detects the property, because both produce a

   306	exercised; both reds were real, and only one was about the fixture. Same experiment, different subject.
   307	
   308	**The expected error text identifies the subject of the experiment.** This is the third independent reason to
   309	assert the code and location rather than "it fails to compile": one lane found its own mis-aimed control by
   310	reading what its fixture expected. A bare compile failure cannot tell you where to aim.

   315

   326	found it by counting stale-versus-correct rather than trusting that "clean" meant clean of the right things.
   327	
   328	## Numbers, artifacts and identity
   329	
   330	**A number that passes through a relay stops being a measurement and becomes a quotation.** Quoting yourself
   331	is how a stale count survives its own correction: a figure measured before a final edit was relayed twice and
   332	was wrong at both stops. Re-derive every count you pass on, or mark it explicitly as unverified relay.
   333	
   334	**Every count names the baseline it was measured against.** "Two files" and "forty files" were both true of

   337	
   338	**Verify by type, not by appearance. Format is not identity.** A well-formed wrong value announces nothing: a

   341	within an hour, and one was caught only by recognising a constant by sight, which is not a control.
   342	
   343	**An echoed value proves a lane read the brief, not that it examined the thing.** Declared = echoed =
   344	**re-derived from the tree** is three checks and only the third is evidence.
   345

   347	states it is materially stronger than running the document's command; agreement then comes from two
   348	directions instead of one.
   349	
   350	**Count by field, not by pattern, and suspect your own instrument first.** A regex census read 50 rows where
   351	there were 52, because two status cells carried a trailing qualifier.
   352	
   353	**Every artifact that certifies a tree carries that tree's identity inside it**, so a copy cannot certify a
   354	different tree by being found in the right place. A superseded lane's genuine `PASS` reading as current is a
   355	live failure mode, not a contrived one.
   356	
   357	**Any location a consumer looks up by convention needs an identity in the name**, or a leftover answers for a
   358	producer that never ran. Proven on three surfaces in one night: an evidence package whose squash message
   359	belonged to the previous block, a results directory, and a gate log whose stale twin carried `rc=127` from
   360	the day before. **A missing artifact asks a question; a stale one answers it.**
   361	
   362	**A command written into a coverage document is a citation, and a citation a reader cannot open is worse than
   363	none.** Run every documented command verbatim out of the file. One document shipped a digest command that
   364	would have produced a *mismatch* for anyone who ran it — correct behaviour reading as a broken verdict, which
   365	manufactures a false finding inside the one document meant to be trusted.
   366	
   367	**Put the explanation where the reader lands, not where it belongs.** A correct account in a file opened
   368	second fails exactly as a stale filename does.
   369	**Repairing a blind instrument has two obligations, and the second is the one that gets skipped: the
   370	instrument must be able to see, and the place you put it must be somewhere the gate looks.** A fix
   371	that relocates a blind fixture into an excluded package is *indistinguishable from a fix* — the
   372	fixture is correct, its control passes, and nothing ever runs it. Verify inclusion by reading the
   373	exclusion list, never by assuming it because most packages are included.
   374	
   375	**A structural argument that bounds a population beats a scan that enumerates it.** Seventeen source
   376	hits on a removed crate name were dismissed without inspection: a live reference could not compile
   377	without the dependency, so every survivor is necessarily a comment. That argument cannot go stale the
   378	way a seventeen-file review can.
   379	
   380	## What an instrument is allowed to prove
   381	
   382	**A prohibition describes a route; the property describes the destination.** Forbidding the three
   383	known ways to reach a bad state leaves the fourth. State the property that must hold and enforce it
   384	where it can be observed, or the instrument ages into a list of the routes someone once thought of.
   385	
   386	**Make the counted path structurally hard to leave.** Three sub-blocks in one block defeated the same
   387	warning by three different mechanisms, none of them illegitimate on its own. When leaving the
   388	instrumented path is easy and silent, the instrument measures compliance rather than behaviour.
   389	
   390	**A cache key that is a strict subset of what determines correctness is a wrong-answer generator**,
   391	not a stale-answer risk. It returns a confidently wrong result for an input it has never seen and
   392	believes it has.
   393	
   394	**Prefer a counter to a boolean.** A boolean records that something happened; a counter records how
   395	often, which is what distinguishes "fired once as designed" from "fires on every request". Several
   396	instruments here were sized from a boolean and answered the wrong question.
   397	
   398	**A rationale can be written from belief; a falsifier cannot be written without knowing the fact it
   399	turns on.** This is why requiring a falsifier produces work before anything is falsified: the author
   400	must find the fact in order to write the sentence.

   704	
   705	**A proof gap may ratify as a recorded unmet obligation. An internal contradiction or a false command
   706	claim may not.** The first states honestly what is not yet established and leaves it visible; the
   707	second asserts something untrue about the artifact or about what a command does, and ratifying it

   710	**Naming a Git object identifies a set; it does not resolve one.** A rationale claiming a named

   714

   716	reopened block traces to it, and it is committed by every kind of participant — implementers,
   717	reviewers, block owners and the orchestrator alike. Treat it as environmental, not as a failing of
   718	whoever committed it most recently.

   729	two: a generator whose transcript write failed left the previous file in place, so a hash comparison
   730	saw equality and read it as success — the failure invisible precisely because nothing changed. Ask

   734	handles the reported case and leaves the next one is a ladder with no top; the recurrence is evidence
   735	the property is unbounded. Sweep the range and name the residual bound in the test, so the limit is a
   736	declared constant rather than wherever the last review happened to stop.

   742	toward reading a green run as evidence for the property it was cited for.

   747	in for the property, fixtures standing in for a universe, and a cross-check that does not exist.

   761	as intent reads identically to "it accumulated" said as observation, and two branches described as one
   762	line turned out to be siblings sharing only their fork point — with the criteria a precondition named

   772

   797

   799	criterion.** One rebind versus two is a heuristic; a digest that does not match its bytes is a defect.
   800	Reach for the count only where correctness does not decide.

  1086	doing — it is not prevention.
  1087	
  1088	**A rule stated for others and not applied to oneself is the recurring signature.** The document that
  1089	taught this one already required invoking an owner rather than partially restating it, "because
  1090	omissions become invisible" — for an external cell, while restating its own facts throughout. Four
  1091	findings that looked like a family of related defects were this single one at four scales.
  1092	
  1093	**Amending a record forward is not fabricating one backward.** Adding a row that states what is
  1094	pinned as of now is ordinary maintenance; creating a record of a lock that never existed is
  1095	retroactive history. They are different acts and the objection to the second does not reach the
  1096	first — conflating them blocked the legitimate move for two rounds.
  1097	
  1098	The discipline that catches it is one question, asked of your own claim before anyone else reads it:
  1099	**what exactly did this examine, and is that the same as what I am about to say?** Where the answer
  1100	is uncertain, the claim is settled by the compiler, a tool, or an independent reader — self-review
  1101	does not qualify, because self-review shares the premise.
  1102	
  1103	## One trap worth stating
  1104	
  1105	**A check that enumerates or matches from the same source it validates proves nothing.** A totality
  1106	test iterating its own map, a residue check reusing the pattern it verifies, or a drift check
  1107	comparing against the recorded sha it is checking, cannot fail for the case it exists to catch.
  1108	Verify against an independent oracle: the directory, not the list; the shape, not the pattern; the
  1109	live tree, not the pinned baseline.
  1110	
  1111	## Preconditions, boundaries and authorisation
  1112	
  1113	**A precondition that runs concurrently with what it must precede is not a precondition — it is a race that
  1114	usually wins.** Three instances in one session, all orchestrator-side: a freeze announced at current trunk
  1115	while the candidate's base sat one commit behind; a health check verified before the final write; a reader
  1116	registration in flight while the seat was already reading. Each usually works, which is why none looked like
  1117	a defect until it cost something.
  1118	
  1119	**A precondition verified before the last mutation is verified against a tree that no longer exists.**
  1120	Recording the verdict is itself a write. The final health check runs after the final write, including that
  1121	one — otherwise a lane certifies a tree that cannot be committed.
  1122	
  1123	**Announce a freeze at the candidate's base, not at current trunk.** A hold announced at "current trunk" is a
  1124	hold on future movement; the first thing it protects is the gap.
  1125	
  1126	**In a fixpoint lane a moving trunk costs a whole lane, not a rebase.** The fast-forward needs a rebase, the
  1127	rebase moves the freeze, and the verdict is void. Everywhere else drift is a delay. Rebase, then freeze.
  1128	
  1129	**Declare a lane's subject as an explicit path set, plus a content digest, before it runs**, and repeat it in
  1130	the receipt beside the reviewed sha. It costs nothing while the brief is being written and converts the next
  1131	drift from an argument into one command. **The difference between a bounded verdict and a post-hoc excuse is
  1132	entirely when the boundary was written down.** A boundary drawn around a result already in hand is not a
  1133	boundary, however true the facts inside it are.
  1134	
  1135	**A declared boundary that never refuses anything is indistinguishable from no boundary.** A lane that stops
  1136	rather than widening is the evidence that the boundary bound. Widen deliberately, declare the new subject
  1137	before restarting, and never let a lane decide its own scope after a result.
  1138	
  1139	**Verify an exclusion; do not accept the claim.** Filtering the excluded path and counting what remains is
  1140	one command, and it is the difference between a claim and a fact.
  1141	
  1142	**A precondition expressed as a failing test beats one expressed as an obligation** — it discharges when a
  1143	named assertion goes green rather than when someone judges the work done. It carries three things or it
  1144	becomes the weakest form instead of the strongest: the named test, proof it is currently red **for the right
  1145	reason**, and an explicit bar on editing it. The cheapest way to make a failing test pass is to change it.
  1146	
  1147	**No landing authorisation without the review mandates named and bound to the candidate sha.** A census is
  1148	not a mandate; a gate is not a mandate; an admissible verdict is not a mandate. This program landed a block
  1149	that had none of the three, on a readiness report that carried everything except the answer to the first
  1150	question the ledger asks — and nobody asked across two rounds and a returned candidate, because **strong
  1151	evidence of one kind reads as sufficiency.** A weaker package would have prompted the question.
  1152	
  1153	**Read an ambiguous grant as the narrower one.** "Proceed under the usual authorisation" was written loosely
  1154	and read as the stop it should have been.
  1155	
  1156	**A record of a refusal is worth most exactly where the refusal was hardest**, so state what was declined,
  1157	what made it attractive, and what accepting would have cost. A refusal carries information in proportion to
  1158	how nearly it went the other way; anyone can record declining something obviously wrong.
  1159	
  1160	**Every discarded verdict records why it was discarded, in the artifact.** The thread dies with the session.
  1161	A later reader meeting the same condition needs the reasoning and the check, not a precedent for waving one
  1162	through.
  1163	
  1164	**A STOP is not a verdict.** A stopped run's silence covers strictly more than the condition it named: it
  1165	reports one failure, and the absence of others reads as everything-before-was-fine when everything *after* is
  1166	simply unexamined. Re-verification after a STOP starts at the beginning, never at the stop point.
  1167	
  1168	**Landed-and-unaccepted is an honest state that no status field can express** — so the row's text has to.
  1169	Never advance a status to match a landing.
  1170	
  1171	## Agent plumbing
  1172	
  1173	**A nested agent cannot address its dispatcher unless the address is in its brief.** Otherwise a completed
  1174	success reads to the waiting seat as indefinite silence — a failure mode invisible on the successful path.
  1175	
  1176	**A register entry that cannot be matched to reality cannot answer the question the register exists to
  1177	answer.** Put the agent id in the row; a row without one reads as a stray.
  1178	
  1179	**Register, then dispatch.** Everything that must be true before an actor starts happens before it starts,
  1180	not alongside.
  1181	
  1182	## Deferrals and design lanes
  1183	
  1184	**A deferral's stated cost is only as complete as the inventory available when it was taken.** One
  1185	deferral recorded two bounded consequences, honestly and as completely as it could be stated. A later
  1186	file-by-file mapping found four files with no covering owner — a cost nobody could have written down,
  1187	because the inventory did not exist yet. **"State the cost carefully" does not prevent this.** What
  1188	prevents it is a trigger: **re-state a deferral's cost whenever new inventory touches its scope**,
  1189	because nothing announces the divergence — the deferral row still reads exactly as it did when it was
  1190	right.
  1191	
  1192	**Do not give orphaned files their own owner to close a coverage gap.** Files map to a deferred unit
  1193	because that unit is the work that touches them; splitting them out manufactures one body of work
  1194	across two decompositions. Undefer the unit, or leave the gap named and open.
  1195	
  1196	**A design lane that can edit source will resolve a hard design question by writing one.** So a task
  1197	whose real content is design is dispatched as design, forbidden from editing source, settled by its
  1198	owner, and only then implemented. An implementation lane running against an unsettled design reaches
  1199	for whatever makes the gate green — one produced a cache that returned before the parse counter, which
  1200	is a design answer written as a bug.
  1201	
  1202	**A task that needs a design decision is a design task however it is written up.** Recognise it by
  1203	what it must decide, not by what the plan calls it.
  1204	
  1205	## Identity of work, not of branches
  1206	
  1207	**A duplicate check keyed on branch NAME cannot see the same work under a second name at a different
  1208	base.** Two refs held one body of work — 53 of 54/55 delta entries shared, the same deletions, the
  1209	same gate — and looked like two independent lines. Compare **delta against each ref's own base**, not
  1210	tree against tree: a tree diff conflates base drift with content and reports divergence that is not
  1211	there. Run a control against an unrelated branch so the shared count means something.
  1212	
  1213	**Establish supersession by body, never by name, date or branch status.** A reverted branch carrying a
  1214	byte-identical file is a copy, not a third instrument; a fixture asserting the identical error on the
  1215	identical symbol is subsumed, not merged.

     1	# Review — three phases, not repeated panels
     2	
     3	## 1. Discovery
     4	
     5	**One** independent review against a frozen slice. Lanes are selected by risk — correctness;
     6	architecture conformance; adversarial challenge of specification, scope and simplicity; a specialist
     7	lane only where concurrency, security or performance genuinely applies.
     8	
     9	Reviewers are blind to each other's findings. A low-risk candidate does not get a full panel.
    10	
    11	## 2. Closure
    12	
    13	The manager verifies findings before they block. **A finding blocks only when all four hold:**
    14	
    15	- supported by concrete evidence or a realistic reproduction;
    16	- introduced or exposed by this candidate;
    17	- within the block's responsibility;
    18	- material to correctness, safety, architecture or acceptance.
    19	
    20	Confirmed **P0/P1** findings go to the implementer as **one deduplicated minimal fix packet**;
    21	P2/P3 are carried, never forwarded. The reviewer
    22	that raised a finding may be resumed to verify that finding and its delta — targeted verification,
    23	not a fresh review. Do not rerun the panel after every fix.
    24	
    25	## 3. Acceptance
    26	
    27	After confirmed findings are closed, **one fresh review of the final frozen candidate** by an agent
    28	that has not seen it. It receives the charter, architecture and final diff — not prior conclusions —
    29	and looks for missed defects and integration problems. A high-risk candidate may get one additional
    30	targeted lane.
    31	
    32	## Acceptance is not reopened later — two checks that prevent it
    33	
    34	Reopening an accepted block is expensive and always has the same two causes.
    35	
    36	**A criterion that names a document requires a verified correspondence to that document.** Not "this
    37	bullet covers it" — an actual comparison, clause by clause, recorded. A block once satisfied
    38	"distinct identity types from the architecture document" with types that collapsed four of that
    39	document's variants into one, losing two identity distinctions. Every review passed, the criterion
    40	looked met, and the divergence surfaced only when a later block became the first consumer and found
    41	the contract's invariant inexpressible. A coverage mapping would not have caught it: the mapping was
    42	correct. What was missing was anyone reading the two side by side. Divergence found this way is
    43	recorded as a deviation for ratification, never resolved silently in either direction.
    44	
    45	**An artifact with no consumer has no evidence, and acceptance says so.** The same type had zero
    46	production callers, so no test could fail and none did. Compilation proved only that it was
    47	well-formed. Where a block delivers something nothing yet uses, its acceptance states that plainly
    48	rather than resting on a green gate that never exercised it — and names what would exercise it.
    49	
    50	## Sub-blocks — decompose so a review can finish
    51	
    52	**A block too large to review in one pass is decomposed into sub-blocks before implementation, by an
    53	architecture consult.** The consult owns the decomposition: each sub-block digestible, independently
    54	reviewable, and bounded so a reviewer can hold all of it at once. A block orchestrator does not
    55	self-decompose — the point is a boundary drawn by someone who is not implementing it.
    56	
    57	**Up to three review rounds per sub-block.** Then it is done, or it is escalated — not carried into
    58	the next sub-block.
    59	
    60	**When every sub-block is complete, the manager runs one conformance and one adversarial pass over
    61	the whole block.** Sub-block reviews establish each part; that final pair establishes that the parts
    62	compose, and it is where cross-sub-block defects are caught. Neither pass substitutes for the other,
    63	and neither substitutes for the sub-block reviews.
    64	
    65	## When rounds are the wrong instrument
    66	
    67	**A complete list closes its class and says nothing about any other.** Eighty-three enumerated
    68	restatements were repaired to two, and two internal contradictions then surfaced for the first time in
    69	twenty-three rounds — they had never been enumerated, so no amount of repairing against that list
    70	could reach them. That sharpens the enumeration thesis rather than weakening it: enumerate the class
    71	you intend to close, and do not read its closure as coverage of another.
    72	
    73	**Iterative repair on a large interlocking document can introduce defects as fast as it removes
    74	them.** Where a count plateaus and new findings trace to previous rounds' own edits, the method is the
    75	suspect, not the effort. Pre-register the disconfirming result before the next round runs — and treat
    76	reaching it as a question about the method rather than a failure of the block, the same shape as
    77	stopping rounds that cannot enumerate.
    78	
    79	**An explanation can be true and insufficient.** One block's non-convergence was diagnosed as
    80	resampling a proper subset, and a stop was lifted on that basis for one enumeration over the correct
    81	universe. The sweep was genuinely better — 1715 rows across 50 artifacts against 1164 across 21 — and
    82	an independent lane then found roughly thirteen more of the same species. The diagnosis accounted for
    83	the 39% nobody had examined and did not account for defects surviving a complete enumeration of the
    84	right population.
    85	
    86	**Accept-as-debt covers claims wider than their evidence, and nothing else.** A present-tense
    87	assertion that a ratified act has already settled is stale with an authority behind it, not imprecise
    88	— that gets a ruling, not a debt row. Getting the disposition right for the right reason matters,
    89	because the wrong reason sends the next instance to the wrong instrument.
    90	
    91	**A lifted stop that produces a better result and still does not converge is the outcome most likely
    92	to be filed as progress.** Say both halves: it was better, and it was not sufficient. Where a surface
    93	has now failed to converge under two explanations, the disposition for its prose class is
    94	accept-as-debt with the residue named — never a further round. Structural findings close regardless
    95	and are not folded into that debt: a gate whose reach is narrower than its claim is not prose drift,
    96	and a row proven against a different candidate is not a wording defect.
    97	
    98	**Never judge convergence on count.** One block's finding counts across nine rounds ran 5, 5, 6, 4,
    99	5, 6, 7, 6, 6 — flat, and by that measure nine rounds of nothing. Underneath, its blockers went from
   100	six against legacy text to two against text written in the previous round, and its dominant class from
   101	eighty-three occurrences to two. A convergence judgement on count would have been correct by its own
   102	measure and wrong in fact.
   103	
   104	**Read where findings land, not only how many.** Findings against a document's newest additions are
   105	convergence on a moving front; findings against legacy text mean the population is still unenumerated.
   106	A round falling from a dominant class to two of six, with both blockers against work written since the
   107	previous round, says the repair held — which the count alone does not.
   108	
   109	
   110	**A population no one has enumerated cannot be cleared by sampling it.** One block's surface held 47
   111	non-owner restatements; a review round finds one to six. That is roughly twenty rounds, and twenty-one
   112	had run without converging — not for want of reviewer or repair quality, but because rounds were the
   113	wrong instrument at any quality. Enumerate the population, then repair the class.
   114	
   115	**An inventory column is evidence, not a verdict.** Applied literally it manufactures findings —
   116	most flagged identity bindings were correct by construction, since a plan must define a derived
   117	identity before it exists. Discarding it loses the class. The defect was narrower than the column: a
   118	derived identity used as the *pin* for a measurement or a source location.
   119	
   120	**A receipt's count is a claim about what the producer found, never about what it delivered.** An
   121	enumeration reported 477 rows and 47 findings and delivered 120 rows containing 9, with its prompt
   122	already requiring it to declare truncation. Counting the artifact's own rows against its receipt is
   123	what exposed it, so require both numbers — rows found and rows listed — and a truncation flag when
   124	they differ. This is the truncation family again, and the first instance where the truncation was in
   125	the producer rather than the reader.
   126	
   127	**Treat a predicate miss as formatting before treating it as absence.** A receipt delivered as a
   128	table rather than marker lines read as zero results. Require markers at column one.
   129	
   130	## Ask a reviewer to defeat a gate, not to check it
   131	
   132	**A reviewer asked to check a gate reads it; a reviewer asked to defeat it runs it.** Set the task as
   133	construction: make this gate pass while something it exists to catch is broken. That found a totality
   134	check asking whether each scope item had at least one row rather than whether that item's obligations
   135	were present — ten of eleven rows could be deleted and the gate stayed admissible.
   136	
   137	**A gate that cannot fail invalidates every result it ever produced.** Not only the current one: each
   138	earlier pass was weaker than it was reported to be, so fixing it means re-running everything it
   139	cleared. Half-fixing it is worse than leaving it alone, because the passes then split into two classes
   140	nobody can tell apart.
   141	
   142	**An instruction is evidence about what its sender believed when they wrote it, never about the
   143	current state.** Refuse one that a later verdict has overtaken, and say which verdict overtook it.
   144	
   145	## Review churn — stop the reviewer prospecting
   146	
   147	**A reviewer may always find a new path.** But if two consecutive rounds surface previously-unexamined
   148	paths, the surface is not being enumerated and further rounds will keep finding more.
   149	
   150	**At that point, stop reviewing and dispatch a low-effort consult to enumerate the remaining paths.**
   151	Its output is the surface; review resumes against it. Enumeration is cheaper than discovery repeated
   152	per round, and it converts an unbounded sequence of rounds into a bounded one.
   153	
   154	## Documents get two rounds
   155	
   156	**A document gets at most two review rounds. Then it ratifies with its residue recorded, or it is
   157	rescoped.** Only a contradiction or a false claim blocks ratification; a proof gap, a wide phrasing,
   158	an underspecified field are recorded as open findings and the plan proceeds.
   159	
   160	A plan is a means. A block's deliverable is the code, and a document polished past two rounds is
   161	spending the block's budget on the wrong artifact — one plan took twenty-three ratification rounds and
   162	eight repair rounds while the cutover it gated had not started. Iterative repair on a large
   163	interlocking document introduces defects at roughly the rate it removes them, so the rounds do not
   164	converge; they circulate.
   165	
   166	## Convergence
   167	
   168	**Default maximum: two substantive fix cycles per slice.** Not converging means stop and rescope,
   169	replace a failing agent, or request an architecture decision — never buy another round.
   170	
   171	**Every third round, an architecture consult joins the next cycle.** Not to review the candidate
   172	again — to ask why three rounds have not closed it. Three failed cycles on one slice is evidence
   173	about the approach, not about the fixes: the same defect class keeps reappearing in new instances,
   174	or the mechanism cannot express what its criterion requires, or the work sits with an owner who
   175	cannot finish it. A fix cycle cannot see any of those, because it is looking at the finding.
   176	
   177	The consult is given the round history and the findings, and asked what is producing them. Its answer
   178	shapes the next cycle rather than being another verdict on the current one.
   179	
   180	**The cap is a signal, never a reason to land or supersede a block that can be made correct.** It
   181	exists because repeating a round that is not working wastes a lane; it does not exist to force a
   182	block out of the program. Where the work is genuinely closable and the only obstacle is a round
   183	count — the block's own or this one — the count is lifted and the block continues until it is
   184	correct. Superseding a block that could have finished, or landing one that is not finished, are both
   185	worse outcomes than another round. Rescope when the approach is wrong; lift the limit when only the
   186	budget is.
   187	
   188	## Reviewer calibration
   189	
   190	Every reviewer dispatch says this, because reviewers otherwise inflate:
   191	
   192	- The objective is finding real defects, **not maximising findings. Reporting none is acceptable.**
   193	- Severity is impact × likelihood — not confidence, and not tone.

   195	  path. An architectural preference is not an architecture violation.
   196	- Pre-existing and out-of-scope issues are recorded separately and never silently expand the block.
   197	- Minor issues and suggestions do not block by default.
   198	- No praise, no generic summary, no unrelated recommendations.
   199	- Recommend the **smallest sufficient fix**, never a redesign.

   201	Each potentially blocking finding carries: location; the violated requirement or invariant; a
   202	concrete failure path; evidence or reproduction; whether this change introduced it; whether it is in
   203	scope; calibrated severity; the minimal sufficient fix.
   204	
   205	**A blocking severity requires direct reproduction, incontrovertible evidence, or independent
   206	verification before an implementer is interrupted.**
   207	
   208	## What a review does not cover
   209	
   210	**A review answers the question it was asked, not the document it was pointed at.** An artifact can
   211	accumulate passing rounds while a false sentence inside it is never in any lane's frame. A claim in
   212	an evidence document survived three rounds — a categorical assertion that a count-only canary could
   213	not catch a regression, contradicted by that block's own measured delta — because every lane was
   214	scoped to the tests and none to the prose.
   215	
   216	So prose claims are unreviewed however many rounds the artifact survived, unless a lane was scoped to
   217	the prose explicitly. Where a document's assertions are load-bearing, scope a lane to them and say so.
   218	
   219	**A PASS with zero blockers is not readiness while findings are open.** Dispositioning carried
   220	findings is new work, not a further fix cycle, and a candidate is not ready until each is adopted,
   221	deferred with its owner and gate named, or rejected with evidence.
   222	
   223	## Dispatch invariants for a lane
   224	
   225	**Pin every diff range to a frozen sha or the merge-base, never a moving branch name.** A lane told to
   226	diff against a branch that advances mid-review reports the candidate DELETING whatever the branch
   227	ADDED — the most alarming finding class there is, a block appearing to destroy someone else's work.
   228	It has cost the opening minutes of two triages to disprove, and it is entirely an artifact of the
   229	range.
   230	
   231	**State the universe and its selection criterion before sweeping, and justify it against what the
   232	block is answerable for — never against what its diff contains.** A sweep whose universe was one
   233	block's changed files read exactly like a complete sweep: same enumerator, same per-item evidence,
   234	same completeness claim. The universe is the one part a report never checks, so a complete sweep of
   235	the wrong universe is indistinguishable from a complete one.
   236	
   237	**A different universe is a first round, not a fourth.** Where a convergence stop was calibrated on
   238	resampling a proper subset, iterative repair was never under test and the stop does not apply to the
   239	first sweep over the correct set.
   240	
   241	**Fixing a broken gate is never "repair" under a no-repair stop.** A stop halts work on the artifact,
   242	never on the instrument — every verdict a broken instrument issued means less than it says, including
   243	the verdicts the stop itself rests on. One existence check matched only executables while its register
   244	named eighteen markdown proofs, so eighteen of thirty rows certified without being opened, and a

   246	
   247	## Result contract
   248	
   249	Every reviewer ends its output with exactly this block, and writes the two marker lines nowhere else:
   250	
   251	    ===VERTER-RECEIPT-BEGIN===
   252	    LANE: <this reviewer's lane>
   253	    RESULT: <PASS|FAIL>
   254	    REVIEWED: <the sha reviewed>
   255	    FINDINGS: <n, or the word none>
   256	    FINDING <id> | <P0|P1|P2|P3> | <file>:<line> | <one-line summary>

   258

   260	
   261	`PASS` means no P0/P1. `FAIL` names what blocks. P2 and below are recorded and carried.
   262	
   263	**Severity is defined, not felt.** P0: data loss, a security or fail-open hole, or demonstrated
   264	incorrect behaviour on an input a user would actually hit — demonstrated, not reachable in
   265	principle. P1: a broken named invariant, a demonstrated race, a second implementation of something

   269	P1 block; P2 and P3 are carried and dispositioned later.**

   275	**A receipt relocated so that it validates must be proven byte-identical to the original.** Re-filing

   281	
   282	**`ALL SOUND` is a verdict about form, not outcome.** A `FAIL` is a sound result. A readiness claim

   292	**Name the class, not the finding.** A prompt pointing at the row where a defect was found tests
   293	whether that fix landed. A prompt stating the defect as a general check — an invariant narrower or
   294	wider than the gate its document names — tests whether the class is gone, and only the second finds
   295	instances nobody has seen. Give the seat the surface and the questions; keep the block's conclusions
   296	out of it.
   297	
   298	**Before carrying a citation forward, open it.** A cite that no reader can follow reads as a
   299	transcription error rather than as the deletion it records, and a finding whose only carrier died
   300	with a branch needs its live carrier named instead of its dead one reproduced.
   301	
   302	
   303	**A seat that can only choose among the offered options will choose among them.** Give every consult
   304	an explicit escape — if the information does not determine the answer, say so and say what would —
   305	or a forced choice comes back looking like a finding.
   306	
   307	**Supply the facts, not the inference.** Give the assignments and let the pattern be reachable;
   308	naming it as a precedent tells the seat what to conclude. Never state a distinction as an argument
   309	toward an answer when it can be stated as a fact about the subject, and never frame a choice as
   310	binary when a third shape is available from the same facts.
   311	
   312	## Model routing
   313	
   314	Capabilities, not model names. Keep assignments here rather than repeated across prompts.
   315	
   316	| Lane | Default | Note |
   317	|---|---|---|
   318	| correctness, bug detection, architecture conformance | Codex | prime with the exact architecture documents; explicitly forbid severity inflation and scope expansion |
   319	| adversarial challenge of assumptions, spec, simplicity, scope | Opus | not the sole bug detector |
   320	| broad exploration, inexpensive second opinion | Grok, optional | not a sole correctness gate |
   321	
   322	Use max-effort settings only where judgment or risk justifies them. Routine coordination, status
   323	handling and mechanical work use cheaper settings.

Publishing an artifact lowers ZERO declaration bodies. First-touch singleflights per `(space, scope, name)` entry; sibling backfill is coverage-gated (only symbols whose FULL header contributor set was lowered populate). A content edit produces a fresh memo — superseded bodies can never serve a new-content demand; overlay artifacts own their own memo, never the base's.

Retention is LEASE-PINNED, not LRU/budget-evicted: the cold-index parse acquires ONE `SnapshotLease` for the artifact's `(canonical, whole_hash, parse_env_hash)` key and hands it to the artifact's `DeclBodyMemo`, so the header-index parse and every later body / whole-env / raw-surface demand reuse that ONE parse for the artifact's whole life — a live artifact never silently re-parses. The lease drops with the memo (hence the artifact), releasing the retained `Rc<ParsedEvalProgram>`. The temporary OXC parse arena stays on the worker (native) / the wasm thread-local shard, is per-file and per-version only, never crosses a thread boundary, and must not leak into long-lived `Send + Sync` shared caches; jobs return owned typed IR.    302	## Semantic Heuristic Prevention (CRITICAL)
   303	
   304	Semantic behavior must be driven by typed facts, explicit projection policy, and complete semantic query identity. Do not encode type meaning, resolver routing, cache validity, or published component-meta shape in local heuristics.
   305	
   306	Forbidden patterns:
   307	
   308	- Inferring semantic meaning from rendered type strings, raw source slices, identifier suffixes/prefixes, path substrings, display text, or compatibility formatting.
   309	- Choosing between candidate type results with subjective "better shape" scoring when the candidates do not carry exactness/provenance proving which one is authoritative.
   310	- Letting projection mode, substitution environment, conditional context, scope version, workspace/source generation, package-boundary policy, or solver options affect a result without being represented in semantic identity, cached-value validation/read-set metadata, or the projection plan.
   311	- Treating numeric caps, recursion limits, or fanout fuses as normal semantic answers. A fuse may stop work, but must return a structured degraded result such as `BudgetExceeded`, `Unsupported`, or an explicit recursion sentinel, and that result must not be promoted into a warm shared cache entry as if complete.
   312	- Adding compatibility or transition paths that preserve old heuristic behavior. Replace the old path with a typed producer fact, a richer IR variant, an explicit policy enum, or a structured unsupported result.
   313	
   314	Allowed optimization heuristics are limited to performance triage that cannot change observable meaning: skipping a cache lookup, choosing an equivalent fast path after tests prove equivalence, or deciding a result is not safe to cache. If an optimization can change which type is returned, which members are visible, how aliases are preserved, or whether a result is considered complete, it is not an optimization heuristic; it is semantic policy and must be modeled explicitly.
   315	
   316	Best-architecture target:
   317	
   318	- Every semantic query has typed identity plus validation metadata covering all meaning-affecting dimensions: declaration identity, scope/version root, projection mode, type arguments/substitution environment, conditional context, package/workspace policy, solver options. The cache may split these between slot key, per-mode entry, and cached-value fact signature, but no dimension may be implicit.
   319	- Every semantic result carries enough exactness/provenance to distinguish `Exact`, `SurfaceOnly`, `Unsupported`, `BudgetExceeded`, and recursion-sentinel outcomes without re-inspecting text or shape.
   320	- Projection planning is explicit. Callers request identity/navigation/shallow/expanded behavior and package-boundary/depth policy up front; resolvers do not infer these from ad hoc shape checks.
   321	- If the current IR cannot represent a TypeScript construct, extend the IR/schema or return a structured unsupported result with diagnostics. Do not recover meaning by reparsing display text.
   322	
   323	## Typed Degradation And Completeness Contract (CRITICAL)
   324	
   325	Semantic degraded states are part of the type system contract. They must be typed, propagated, and observable.
   326	
   327	- `TypeExpr::Unknown(UnknownValue)` is not a carrier for semantic control flow. Misses, unsupported intrinsics/operators, alias cycles, recursion sentinels, budget exits, unstable-state exits, and bridge-depth exits must use typed variants or typed sidecar state. Do not encode them as strings such as `"budgetExceeded(...)"` / `"aliasCycle(...)"` and do not recover them with `starts_with` / regex checks.
   328	- `Unknown` is allowed only for a genuine unknown type value with provenance explaining why the producer could not represent it. If the producer knows this is `Unsupported`, `BudgetExceeded`, `Recursive`, `Miss`, or `Unstable`, use that state instead.
   329	- Public query envelopes must preserve completeness. `Complete` means the required inputs were available, current, and no budget/unsupported/unstable branch affected the answer. A query may return `Complete(None)` only when absence itself was proven under the current facts; missing analysis, stale cache data, unavailable providers, unsupported operators, and budget exits must surface as `Unavailable`, `Partial`, or a typed degraded result.
   330	- Degraded results may be displayed and returned to callers, but must not be promoted into warm shared caches as complete answers.
   331	
   332	## Cache Population Target Contract
   333	
   334	Architectural target for the project-global cache cutover:
   335	
   336	- Cache ownership is split into three reusable layers:
   337	  - file artifact caches (`IndexedReady`, prepared declarations, route surfaces, owner import surfaces, optional analysis)
   338	  - semantic query caches (resolved declaration identity, instantiated meaning, indexed access, projected members, mapped or conditional results, normalized reusable intermediates)
   339	  - final result caches (e.g. final component-meta payloads)
   340	- Final payload caches should hand out immutable `Arc` values. Cache backend choice is an implementation detail as long as concurrency, size bounds, and validation rules are preserved.
   341	- Reusable semantic cache population must be path-independent. If the same semantic result is reached through different entry paths, a successful computation must populate the same shared cache entry.
   342	- Broader successful results may backfill narrower reusable entries they actually satisfied.
   343	- Narrower successful results must not claim broader work is cached.
   344	- An `Expanded` result may satisfy and backfill `Shallow` or `Identity` for the same semantic key.
   345	- A `Shallow` result may satisfy and backfill `Identity` for the same semantic key.
   346	- A whole-surface projection may backfill per-member or per-indexed-access caches for the members or accesses it actually materialized.
   347	- A narrow member or indexed-access result must not pretend sibling members or whole-surface projection are cached.
   348	- Cancelled, superseded, interrupted, budget-exceeded, or partial results must not be promoted as warm shared cache entries.
   349	- Versioned semantic nodes and final-result entries must also be sweepable. Project-global caching may be aggressive, but old identities must not accumulate forever across long editing sessions.
   350	- Top-level live-host results must publish through a completion fence: record the touched dependency signature, revalidate before publish, retry at most 3 times on mid-flight changes, never warm shared caches with torn provisional or unstable results.
   351	
   352	Concrete expectation:
   353	
   354	- If `ProjectSurface(C, Expanded)` materializes member `"foo"`, a later `ProjectMember(C, "foo", Expanded)` should reuse that work.
   355	- If `ProjectMember(C, "foo", Expanded)` ran first, that must not imply `ProjectSurface(C, Expanded)` is cached.

   357	## Query Mode Contract
   358	
   359	The shared semantic query system has exactly five modes. Every caller picks one; there is no implicit mode. Every `SemanticQueryKey` carries its mode as part of the cache key.
   360	
   361	- **`Identity`** — return the declaration identity only (canonical file + symbol name + optional substitution environment). Do not read the body; do not walk the decl graph; do not produce a result shape. Cheapest operation. For an alias `type X = Y`, `Identity(X)` returns **`X`'s** declaration identity — not `Y`'s. Used for "does this name resolve" checks and for wiring dependency edges.
   362	- **`Navigate`** — do the minimum semantic work to continue a requested path. Unwrap aliases transparently (aliases have no independent structural shell; `Navigate(X)` where `type X = Y` returns the same node as `Navigate(Y)`), follow member / index hops already materialized in the graph, reduce closed conditionals, stop at undecidability barriers. Does NOT recursively materialize subtrees; does NOT expand sibling members. Used by path projection to step one hop at a time. `Navigate` is one of the entrances of the open-key-domain carrier-stop — see **Open-Key-Domain Carrier-Stop (L1)** below.
   363	- **`Shallow`** — return one shell / one surface level of the requested node without recursive expansion. Object: produce member names + per-member reference nodes; do NOT recurse into member bodies. Conditional: if the check is open / undecidable, expose both branches as references; if closed / decidable, reduce immediately and return only the selected branch shell. Union / intersection: expose contributor references. Alias: unwrap transparently to the target's `Shallow` form (aliases have no structural shell to materialize).
   364	- **`Expanded`** — recursively materialize the requested result. Walk into member bodies, resolve nested references, evaluate every decidable conditional, distribute open conditionals into their remaining path projections, normalize unions / intersections. Aliases: unwrap transparently. Most expensive mode.
   365	- **`Skeleton`** — specialised traversal mode for BFS/generic-helper surfaces where unbound type parameters must remain `TypeParam` shells and conditional branches must not collapse to `never` just because arguments are intentionally absent. It is not a display mode and does not alias `Navigate`; it is a distinct semantic policy.
   366	
   367	**Carrier-preserving decl-body lowering.** Under `ProjectionMode::Shallow` (as under `Navigate` / `Skeleton`), decl-body lowering (`crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/lower.rs`) interns `DeclRef` / `InstantiationRef` carriers for member-value type references — including ALL builtin utilities — and never executes `ResolveDecl` / `Instantiate` eagerly. Under `Navigate` / `Skeleton`, a builtin over an OPEN argument (predicate `raise.rs::builtin_lowering_argument_is_open`: the argument subtree reaches an unbound `TypeParam` — including a mapper binder substituted later at a demand point — or an open carrier) also interns the carrier; closed-argument non-object-filter builtins keep the eager execute. Eager lowering-time execution is `Expanded` / `Identity` only. Materialisation enters exclusively through the demand points: PathWalker hops, the shallow-surface synthesiser's carrier unwrap (`walk.rs::visit_shallow_node` — an `InstantiationRef` unwrap dispatches `Instantiate` under `StructuralTransit(Navigate)` and stamps interface/class bodies as heritage overlays), closed object-filter surface reads, and the relation/conditional oracle (`build.rs::pre_relation_infer_selection` may execute a carrier-check instantiation, pre-evaluating its operator-shaped arguments, to materialise the check for positional infer binding).
   368	
   369	**Query-free structural carrier emission (LIVE macro-arg producer).** A separate, session-owned structural lowerer (`crates/verter_session/src/structural_carrier_producer/macro_arg_producer.rs`, entry `lower_type_expr_structural`, a BARE module-private fn — the producer is COLLAPSED into the ONE private module `crate::structural_carrier_producer::macro_arg_producer`, declared as a private `mod macro_arg_producer;` that re-exports only `macro_type_arg_hot_ref` + `MacroHotMirror` `pub(crate)`; the FOREIGN case is compiler-confined by module privacy and the SAME-MODULE residual is policed by the strengthened single-producer guards) emits the unresolved carriers directly from an owned `TypeExpr`, NodeScopeId-rooted, performing NO name / import / type resolution or reduction — it is a PRODUCER of carriers, never a second resolver, so it neither competes with nor duplicates the single demand-time resolution engine. A bare `Foo` becomes `BareRef`; `Foo<Arg>` a `BareRef` whose `type_args` are structurally lowered (never an `InstantiationRef`); `import("…")` an `ImportType`; unsupported raw syntax a `RawFallback` (display/compat only, never a control-flow miss); a construct-signature type a `Signature { kind: Construct }` node; tuple rest stays on `TupleElement.rest`; and `keyof` / indexed-access / conditional / mapped / `typeof` lower to their deferred shells carrying structurally-lowered operands — even where the eager path would reduce them. The only "resolution" it performs is the purely syntactic in-scope binder lookup that maps a `Ref` to a type-parameter / `infer` binder it already interned. It is intern-only (it never reaches `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, a `CarrierResolverContext`, a `SemanticQueryKey`, or any host / type-provider state) and stays demand-time — never pulled into publish or indexing (the `indexed_ready_publish_lowers_zero_decl_bodies` invariant).    377	The authoritative spec for the L1 carrier-stop: **open key domain ⇒ shallow carrier, route/mode-independent** — it fires in every mode (`Navigate` / `Expanded` / `Shallow` / `Skeleton` / `StructuralTransit`) and no route escapes it. Typed-IR only — no string matching.

Owner predicate: `raise.rs::utility_enumeration_domain_is_open_or_unknown`. Closed sources still materialise the requested keys path-precisely: `Pick<Foo,'bar'>`, `Pick<{bar,baz},'bar'>`, and `Pick<SimpleBox<string>,'icon'>` (a concrete object-bodied generic instantiation) all enumerate. Co-located unit guard (inline in `raise.rs`, not an R6-registry entry): `utility_enumeration_domain_open_for_unbound_generic_closed_for_concrete`.

VALUE-position publication of an open `Pick` still stays a shallow carrier (`chatmessages_resolvable_barrel_publishes_open_pick_as_shallow_carrier`); the surface-position pin is `get_component_meta_chat_messages_shaped_open_pick_heritage_enumerates_picked_keys_only` plus the `pick_over_genuinely_open_source_*` / `pick_over_instantiated_generic_*` regressions in `component_meta_pick_omit_tests.rs`.

   396	
   397	**Tri-state conditionals via the shared oracle.** Conditional closedness routes through `ProjectSemanticDispatch::conditional_branch_selection` — the ONE branch-selection oracle that owns the FULL selection path `build_conditional` reduces with, so build-time reduction and predicate-time classification cannot diverge. Selection order: an `error` check dominates (⇒ Deferred); then the INFER ROUTING (`conditional_infer_route`) — a bare-`infer` extends binds `X := check` THROUGH the sole relation authority for ANY check (pre-`any`-guard placement is load-bearing), an in-scope direct pattern (object property / tuple head-tail / array element / function positions) binds through the relation's inference session, and an exact homomorphic mapped target `{ [P in keyof infer T]: X }` enables the frozen `ReverseHomomorphicMapped` session pass. That pass substitutes the mapper parameter by node identity for each closed source member, routes every property relation back through `execute(Relate)`, reduces substituted conditionals through the canonical conditional query whenever ordinary relation descent reaches them (including nested object, tuple, array, and function positions), records only registered canonical `T[key]` projection deposits, and submits one lower-priority aggregate candidate for `T`. Before any projection deposit, the full bound subtree is scanned through the exhaustive `SemanticNodeData::means_type_is_not_yet_known` classification: unresolved bare/import/`typeof` carriers, `RawFallback`, and failure/degradation `Opaque(QueryError)` variants refuse the deposit, while resolvable `DeclRef`/`InstantiationRef` carriers and the publishable `Opaque(RecursiveRef | DeclPlaceholder)` carriers do not. The reverse-source preflight applies those checks only to positions `assemble_reverse_candidate` can carry into the result: object member values and index-signature keys/values, array elements, and tuple element values; root object call/construct signatures, keyspace, and open-spread operands are not scanned because assembly drops them (open spreads are independently rejected by the root-open guard). The exhaustive subtree edge walk includes free-standing `TypeParam.constraint` / `default` in addition to signature-declared type-parameter bounds. Reverse construction preserves an array or tuple source's readonly container bit; mapped member modifier inversion remains an object-member/index-signature concern. A decided-positive property with no projection candidate recovers `unknown` and marks the aggregate partial, while a failed or `Unknown` property aborts and rolls back the pass. Name remaps, non-`keyof T` key spaces, inactive infer declarations, and other deep infer patterns ⇒ Deferred (never an unbound substitution). Then an `any` check (uses both branches) ⇒ Deferred; then the full relation authority `execute(SemanticQueryKey::Relate)` via `execute_relate_pair` (`Unknown` ⇒ Deferred). The O(tag) fast-reject prefilter lives INSIDE the authority — never consulted as a parallel truth source. A binding-producing selection is always TRUE: `build_conditional` substitutes the relation payload's fixed bindings into the true branch; the closedness classifiers consume a bare-infer binding the same way and widen non-bare shapes to the Deferred treatment (a conservative superset). True-selected classifies ONLY the true branch — an open LOSING branch is dead (guard: `bare_infer_extends_selects_true_through_the_shared_oracle`); False-selected classifies only the false branch; Deferred classifies check/extends value-sensitively plus BOTH branches. The classifier only INVOKES the oracle: operands resolve to nodes solely via environment-free interning (literals/primitives/`infer` placeholders), identity bindings (including default-bound params — guard: `defaulted_type_parameters_bind_their_default_identity` — and wrapper-forwarded bindings — guard: `binding_identity_selects_conditionals_through_concrete_arguments`), and own-scope named-ref resolution (`prepared.name_resolution` → interned `DeclRef`; guard: `closed_named_ref_operands_select_through_the_shared_oracle`); unresolvable operands ⇒ Deferred; the classifier never reimplements assignability and never materialises branches.

OPEN (object-filter domain) ⇒ the walk reaches an unsubstituted `TypeParam`, a deferred conditional with an open operand or branch, an open `IndexedAccess`/`KeyOf`/`Mapped`, an instantiation whose produced KEY SET depends on an open argument per the rules above, an unresolved or open-bodied `DeclRef` alias chain, an `Opaque`, or exhausts the walk budget. Verdicts are memoized per `(node, position)` — a hash-consed repeated open node (`Pick<Foo<T, T>, K>`) stays open on revisit; only in-flight cycle back-edges are closed-for-revisit. CLOSED ⇒ a finite object surface / concrete instantiation (including a nested closed object-filter — `Pick<Pick<{…},'a'|'b'>,'a'>` — and a generic wrapper whose open argument stays in value positions: `type Outer<T> = Foo<T>` and `interface Outer<T> extends Foo<T> {}` both keep `Omit<Outer<T>,'items'>` closed) / a finite union/intersection of those / a concrete-operand operator body (an oracle-selected conditional with a closed selected branch, a K-only remapped mapped type) reached without crossing an open node (a bounded alias chain `Foo→Bar→{bar:string}` resolves CLOSED). An `InstantiationRef` is CLOSED only when its target decl exists with satisfied arity/defaults, every arg/default is closed, AND the prepared body is closed under those bindings. `infer` is a conditional-inference binding placeholder, NOT an unbound generic — it does not open the domain by itself (a decidable `extends UIMessage<infer M, …>` over a concrete check stays closed); an infer name bound by an oracle-selected bare-infer conditional classifies as its bound check. A chained-conditional-bodied concrete source such as `Pick<PropsBase<UIMessage[]>,'icon'>` is NOT L1 carrier-stopped either, but currently yields `semanticMiss` downstream — a separate conditional-reduction gap (a current scoped exception, listed below), NOT an L1 concern (it does NOT materialise the requested keys today).
