   432	**Invalidation.** The closedness walk's cross-file reads (alias-chain hops, barrel re-export hops, prepared-decl bodies) are observed as `FileWholeHash` facts onto the active tracer (`raise.rs::observe_closedness_walk_consult`), so every published carrier/materialised entry's `ReadSetSignature.facts` carries them — an edit that flips a dependency's closedness rejects the warm entry on the read-side validator and the verdict recomputes (guard: `open_pick_carrier_invalidates_when_cross_file_closedness_dependency_flips`).
   433	
   434	**Primary defense + fuse backstop.** The L1 carrier-stop is the PRIMARY defense for the open-generic class at every entrance: a finite-large legitimate published surface decidable as CLOSED terminates on its own merits and is published. The per-request projection budget (`request_budget.rs`) is an ARMED-by-default runaway fuse (`projection_op_budget == 0` ⇒ effective cap 2000); the projection keys plus `Instantiate`/`Conditional` count toward it; an armed fuse that trips returns `BudgetExceeded` as a genuine partial (refused warm admission — the no-poison invariant).
   435	
   436	**Corpus forensics.** The two heaviest real-corpus components terminate fast off the backstop. `Table.vue`'s storm was eager Shallow decl-body lowering recursively executing member-value `Instantiate(StructuralTransit:Shallow)` across the transitive TanStack decl graph, entered once from the macro-payload eval — 94.3% of all budget charges compounding distinct instantiation keys — removed by the carrier-preserving decl-body lowering rule (see Query Mode Contract). `ChatMessages.vue`'s storm was the registry/publication Expanded demand pipeline materialising the open-conditional mapped slots surface — removed by the Navigate-only publication demand (component-meta publication routes record zero `Published(Expanded)` contexts; guard `publication_routes_never_demand_expanded`; ChatMessages resolves in seconds with 0 trips — the no-timeout tracker `chat_messages_resolves_without_timeout` in `defect_b_corpus_prevention_gate.rs` pins it). Both are COMPLETE corpus-set members with un-ignored green trackers (`table_resolves_complete_and_warm`, `chat_messages_resolves_complete_without_false_partial`). Supporting rails: the `TypeOf` query mirrors `Instantiate`'s key convention — an env-bearing content-free `ValueRootSlotIdentity` (T/L/J) plus a dedicated `TypeOfContext { projection_reduction, resolve_env_hash }` (R), derived solely through `ProjectSemanticDispatch::typeof_key_for` (memo slot via `context_to_slot`; key-shape parity with `KeyOf`/`MappedType`); `build_typeof` lowers the value's annotation / object shape / signature surface / enum surface AT the requested demand — a Skeleton/Navigate transit crossing `typeof` of a value typed against a large decl graph gets carriers, never an Expanded build-time materialisation of that graph (the `lower.rs` decl-body sites pass the ambient lowering context, the PathWalker typeof hop passes its own mode — a demand point, operator recursion passes the enclosing context, and the class-surface Static side stays a genuine-Expanded consumer; the overload-visibility projection rule in `build_typeof` is mode-independent; pinned by `typeof_value_graph_lowers_at_requested_demand` + `typeof_macro_payload_publication_stays_bounded`); `TypeOf` counts toward the projection fuse (a demand-bearing projection reducer is fuse-backed); and an admission-REFUSED complete materialise returns the COMPUTED value non-cacheably (`cache_suppress=true`, `result_is_partial` CLEAR — post-compute revalidation refusing a COMPLETE entry is benign non-cacheability, never a partial and never a fabricated `Tainted` substitute; pinned by `admission_revalidation_refusal_is_not_a_partial_result`).
   437	
   438	**Current scoped exceptions (known gaps, by name):**
   439	
   440	1. The un-budgeted raise/convert/drop surface — the raise/convert/drop path does not count toward the projection fuse today (it is a fuse-layer SPLIT-CANDIDATE block); the warm-pass wall-clock residual sits there.
   441	2. The `Pick<PropsBase<UIMessage[]>,'icon'>` chained-conditional `semanticMiss` reduction gap (see OPEN/CLOSED above).
   442	3. The intrinsic/fallthrough `ProjectPath:Published:Expanded` corpus exception — defined by `dispatch_helpers.rs`'s Class-A Expanded fall-through `project_expr_class_a_via_dispatch_threaded` (reached directly or via its non-threaded wrapper `project_expr_class_a_via_dispatch`) and its live callers: `intrinsic_members_for_tag`'s intrinsic/fallthrough composition in `host_manage/intrinsic_projection.rs` (records `ProjectPath:Published:Expanded` charges on the real corpus — measured: 214 on a ChatMessages resolve), the value-expression evaluator in `resolver_core/fallthrough.rs`, the imported-alias registry refinement in `host_manage/component_meta_methods.rs`, the registry materialiser's route-target and `KeyOf` publication sites in `meta_resolve/registry_materialize.rs`, and the JSDoc payload resolution in `host_manage/jsdoc_resolve.rs`. These sites legitimately demand Expanded today and are out of the Navigate-only-publication rule's scope — `publication_routes_never_demand_expanded` covers the projector/registry macro surfaces only; the correct end-state converts this consumer set to Navigate.
   443	4. The view-snapshot false-stale admission refusal — a live-session contributor first parsed mid-request (the `Icon.vue` slot-binding class) fails the materialise admission revalidation deterministically on the first cold request; the unadmitted-value protocol keeps the published result correct (the computed value flows back, non-cacheable, never partial) but warm caching is delayed by one request. The correct end-state snapshots the lazily-parsed contributor into the request view at `ensure_indexed_ready_serve` time (hermetic plain-view pin: `first_cold_request_admits_materialise_whose_contributor_parsed_mid_request`).
   444	
   445	R6-registry guards for the publication surface: `chatmessages_resolvable_barrel_publishes_open_pick_as_shallow_carrier`, `closed_pick_sources_still_materialize_path_precisely`, `projection_budget_counts_instantiate_and_conditional`, `cycle_guard_roots_at_utility_source_type_argument`.
   446	
   447	**Alias boundary preservation.** Although `Navigate` / `Shallow` / `Expanded` unwrap aliases structurally, the alias boundary is preserved on the origin layer via the `AliasResolve` edge kind (see "Derivation / Origin Layer Contract"). Clients needing alias provenance (LSP hover, error messages, compat display) walk that edge; clients needing pure structural meaning ignore it. Each alias hop (direct alias, re-export alias, barrel alias) emits one `AliasResolve` edge; chains are walkable end-to-end.
   448	
   449	**Backfill rule.** Broader successful results may backfill narrower modes for the same key, but ONLY when a recorded materialised point dominates the narrower target (path-exact `cached_satisfies`, never enum rank): an `Expanded` result may satisfy `Shallow`, `Navigate`, and `Identity`; a `Shallow` result may satisfy `Identity` only — NOT `Navigate` (`Shallow ⊅ Navigate`: a one-shell Shallow surface does not materialise a `Navigate` next-hop); a `Navigate` result may satisfy `Identity`. Narrower successful results MUST NOT claim broader modes are cached.
   450	
   451	**Cache topology.** The five modes do NOT imply five separate cache subsystems. `SemanticGraphStore` owns one semantic memo layer. At the semantic-contract level, mode is part of request identity; at the storage level, implementations should group same-base different-mode requests into one memo-entry family (or equivalent single-authority structure) keyed by the mode-erased semantic shape — operation, base identity, path / projection, substitutions, scope, version root — with per-mode slots or equivalent one-way upgrade/backfill semantics. Required behaviour: backfill is directional (broader-projection → narrower-projection) and gated by recorded-point dominance — `Expanded` may satisfy `Shallow` / `Navigate` / `Identity`, `Shallow` may satisfy `Identity` (NOT `Navigate`: `Shallow ⊅ Navigate`), `Navigate` may satisfy `Identity`, and no lower mode may claim a broader mode is cached. `Skeleton` is a separate policy slot; it does not alias `Navigate` or any other mode unless a typed equivalence proof and regression tests justify a backfill edge. Distinct mode requests must not duplicate in-flight authority or split into independent wait graphs.
   452	
   453	**Cache-key distinctness.** `ProjectMember(C, "foo", Shallow)` and `ProjectMember(C, "foo", Expanded)` are distinct cache entries. Generic substitutions are part of the key: `MyType<string>` and `MyType<number>` never alias; two callers reaching `MyType<string>` through different entry paths dedup to one entry. Do not compress mode identity into booleans or partial encodings such as "is navigate"; store the exact `ProjectionMode` or a typed projection-policy key.
   454	
   455	## Path-Precise Navigation And Projection Contract
   456	
   457	Path projection is the default shape of every semantic query. Whole-surface expansion is a degenerate case of projecting the empty path; single-hop `ProjectMember` / `IndexedAccess` are sugar for `ProjectPath` with length 1.
   458	
   459	- **Path queries are first-class semantic queries.** `SemanticQueryKey::ProjectPath { base, path, context }` is the canonical form (`context` is a `ProjectionReductionContext { mode, demand, provenance, merge_role, vue_heritage_policy }` — `provenance`, `merge_role`, and the content-free Vue heritage policy are folded into `FamilyKey` for every context-bearing projection-reduction family; the terminal projection mode rides on `context.mode`).
   460	- **Materialize only subpaths needed for the requested path.** Sibling members and unrelated branches are not touched.
   461	- **Mode cascades along the path.** Intermediate hops run in `Navigate`; only the terminal hop runs in the caller's requested mode (`Shallow`, `Expanded`, or `Identity`).
   462	- **Intersection contribution rule.** When projecting a path through `A & B`, only arms that contribute to the next path segment are projected; non-contributing arms are ignored for that path (not rewritten to `never`). If multiple arms contribute, the projected results of the contributing arms are intersected. Zero contributors is a projection miss.
   463	- **Union contribution rule.** Every union member must contribute to the path; if any member fails the path, the union projection is a union-wide miss.
   464	- **Conditional path rule.**
   465	  - **Closed/decidable conditional** (check resolves deterministically under the current substitution environment): reduce immediately, select the winning branch, continue projecting the remaining path through the selected branch only. Emit `ConditionalSelect` origin.
   466	  - **Open/undecidable conditional** (check depends on free type parameters or unresolved inference): keep the conditional shell and distribute the remaining path **into both branches**, producing a conditional whose branches are per-branch projections. Do NOT short-circuit to an opaque symbolic node as the default behaviour.
   467	  - **Genuine-`Expanded` distribution scope.** A QUERY-ROOT unbound conditional under genuine `Expanded` demand distributes into both branches at the empty-path expander (guard: `root_conditional_still_distributes`). A nested-position open conditional has no reachable genuine-`Expanded` route today — the empty-path expander walks top-level composition only, and the open-mapped carrier-stop owns the mapped-value entrance; the desired carrier behaviour for a future genuine-`Expanded` nested route is pinned by the ignored tracker `nested_open_conditional_not_distributed_under_expanded` (follow-up: genuine-expanded-nested-conditional-carrier).
   468	- **Barrier rule.** Undecidability is the barrier, not the existence of a conditional. An `infer` binding is not itself a barrier; if the enclosing conditional's check is decidable with the current substitution environment, the navigator reduces the conditional and binds `infer` via the relation engine. Only when the check stays open does the conditional form a barrier.
   469	- **Coarse symbolic stop is retired as the default.** The old "open-generic symbolic stop" (`Applied { identity, args }` returned when args are open at depth > 0) is retired for path projection and expansion. Symbolic-stop-style fallback survives only as a **budget-exceeded failure**, signalled explicitly via `BudgetExceededFailure`, never as the main semantic path for open generics.
   470	
   471	Concrete expectations:
   472	
   473	- Navigating `A['c']['full']['bar']` through an object surface touches at most three projection nodes plus the terminal; no unrelated siblings materialize.
   474	- Projecting `OtherType<string>['a']['foo']` through `type OtherType<T> = { a: Foo, b: T } & (T extends string ? S : N)` touches `Foo['foo']` and `S['a']['foo']`; `N` is never walked. `b` is not touched because `'a'` is the requested segment.
   475	- Navigating `OtherType['a']['foo']` with `T` open distributes `['a']['foo']` into both conditional branches, intersects their contributions, and leaves `b` untouched.
   476	
   477	## Navigator Boundary Contract
   478	
   479	Architectural target for the project-global cache cutover:
   480	
   481	- Navigators are not a second resolver. They are thin path-walkers over the shared semantic query system.
   482	- Navigators may perform only non-owning normalization:
   483	  - unwrap already-resolved aliases
   484	  - apply already-known substitutions
   485	  - inspect already-materialized member or keyspace shape
   486	  - choose the next hop in the requested path
   487	- Navigators must not privately perform reusable semantic work such as:
   488	  - recursively resolving a new declaration identity
   489	  - crossing imports or barrel routes
   490	  - instantiating a new generic body outside the query system
   491	  - expanding a mapped, conditional, or indexed-access type through an ad hoc path
   492	  - populating shared caches from outside the shared semantic query API
   493	- Boundary rule: same semantic node may continue inline; a new semantic node must enter through the shared query API.
   494	- Any operation that can recurse, cross files, instantiate meaning, or produce a reusable cached result must be represented as a semantic subquery.
   495	- Prefer enforcing this boundary as a Rust API/trait split, not only as prose. Navigators should not receive owning semantic query operations directly.
   496	
   497	Concrete expectation:
   498	
   499	- While navigating `A['c']['full']['bar']`, the navigator may determine the next hop after `"full"` points at instantiated `C`, but resolving or expanding that instantiated `C` must occur through the shared semantic query layer rather than by private navigator recursion.
   500	
   501	## Generic Navigation And Expansion Contract
   502	
   503	Generic substitutions are part of semantic meaning and therefore part of semantic query identity. Navigation and expansion operate on instantiated meaning, not on the raw generic declaration body alone.
   504	
   505	- Query keys for reusable semantic work must include the relevant type arguments or substitution environment.
   506	- Member projection and indexed access against generic aliases, instantiated types, or mapped helpers must apply substitutions before deciding what member or keyspace is visible.
   507	- If two callers reach the same instantiated semantic node through different entry paths, they converge onto the same cache entry.
   508	- If two callers reach the same declaration name with different type arguments, they do not alias to the same cache entry.
   509	- When a declaration body is navigated in `Navigate` or `Shallow` mode with some type parameters unbound, the resulting graph preserves those parameters as first-class type-parameter references. Clients may later instantiate the preserved graph by applying a substitution environment.
   510	- When a declaration is instantiated with a concrete substitution, every substituted occurrence of a type parameter in the projected result has a `SubstituteTypeParam` edge on the origin layer linking the substituted concrete type back to the parameter's declaration site.
   511	- **Navigation-once invariant.** Navigating `type MyType<T> = …` performs at most one full body lowering per `(decl_identity, whole_hash)`. Later instantiations (`MyType<string>`, `MyType<number>`, …) reuse the parameterized lowering and run only substitution + terminal leaf materialization + branch selection. Distinct concrete instantiations never re-lower the body.
   512	- **Relation-check-once invariant.** For a conditional `T extends S ? A : B`, the relation check runs at most once per distinct check-relevant substitution class. Two instantiations whose substituted check types are identical (e.g., `MyType<string>` called 50 times) run the relation check once.
   513	- **Built-in utilities follow the same semantic model.** `Partial<T>`, `Pick<T, K>`, `Omit<T, K>`, `Record<K, V>`, `ReturnType<F>`, `Parameters<F>`, `ThisParameterType<F>`, `OmitThisParameter<F>`, `Awaited<P>`, `Uppercase`/`Lowercase`/`Capitalize`/`Uncapitalize`, `Extract`/`Exclude`/`NonNullable`, `NoInfer`, and every other built-in utility participate in the same `Instantiate` / `SubstituteTypeParam` / `ProjectMember` / `Normalize` / `ConditionalSelect` / `InferBind` / `AliasResolve` origin model as user-defined aliases and helpers. A utility is not a second semantic class.
   514	- **Utility fast-path rule.** Utility-specific fast paths are permissible only when all three clauses hold: (1) measurably faster than the generic dispatch path on a benchmark fixture, (2) observationally equivalent — same `SemanticNodeId` for the same inputs, same mode / cache behaviour, same `SemanticGraphStats` attribution — to the generic path, (3) emit the **same origin edges** the generic path would have emitted. A fast path that skips edge emission is not allowed; revert to the generic dispatch instead. Optimisation happens only after equivalence is test-enforced.
   515	
   516	Concrete expectations:
   517	
   518	- Navigating `Box<C>['full']['bar']` resolves `"full"` against the instantiated `Box<C>` meaning, not the unsubstituted generic body.
   519	- If `ProjectMember(ResolveDecl(Box), "full", [C])` is already cached, a later path reaching the same instantiated query reuses it.
   520	- Navigating `MyType<T>` with `T` free returns a shape whose body preserves `T` as a parameter reference. Navigating `MyType<string>` returns a shape with `T` substituted, every substituted position carrying a `SubstituteTypeParam` origin edge to the decl's parameter list.
   521	
   522	## Derivation / Origin Layer Contract
   523	
   524	The type graph structurally interns nodes — two distinct derivations producing the same structural result share one arena entry. Origin therefore cannot live inline on each node: the same node may be the result of many derivations. Origin is modelled as a **separate graph layer** of edges from result nodes to their source nodes, co-owned by the `SemanticGraphStore`.
   525	
   526	- Origin edges are stored outside the interned node table, in a sibling edge set keyed by `(result_node, edge_kind, source_node)` with optional per-edge metadata.
   527	- A single result node may have multiple origin edges of the same kind from different derivations; the layer MUST support this. Walking from a result returns the full edge set, not one canonical chain.
   528	- Walking is a first-class API on `SemanticGraphStore`, not a private solver internal. External consumers (component-meta compat, LSP hover, error-message rendering) walk origin to present provenance.
   529	- Origin edges are immutable once published; they participate in the same `ReadSetSignature.facts` fact-signature validation as the interned nodes they point at. Cancelled / budget-exceeded / superseded derivations do not publish origin edges.
   530	
   531	**Required edge kinds** (names are normative; semantics must not drift):
   532	
   533	- **`Instantiate`** — `result = decl<args>`. From the instantiated result back to the declaration identity and concrete argument nodes.
   534	- **`SubstituteTypeParam`** — `result_position = T -> V`. From a concrete type in a substituted position back to the declaration's type parameter and the binding that produced the substitution.
   535	- **`ConditionalSelect`** — `result = select(conditional, True | False | Deferred)`. From the selected-branch result back to the conditional's check, extends, branches, and the deciding relation judgement. Records the branch taken (or `Deferred` if the check stayed open).
   536	- **`InferBind`** — `result = T bound via infer`. From the inferred type back to the `infer` binding site and the concrete type captured by the relation check.
   537	- **`ProjectMember` / `ProjectIndex` / `ProjectPath`** — `result = base.segment(s)`. From the projected result back to the base node and the path segment(s) requested.
   538	- **`Normalize`** — `result = normalize(source_members)`. From a normalized union / intersection / simplified result back to each contributing member node.
   539	- **`AliasResolve`** — `result = unwrap(alias)`. From the unwrapped-target result node back to the alias declaration identity. Emitted once per alias hop (direct alias, re-export alias, barrel alias). Chains are walkable end-to-end so clients can render the full alias provenance.
   540	
   541	Edges compose. `ProjectPath(OtherType<string>, ['a','foo'])` produces a node whose origin traces `ProjectMember → ProjectMember → Instantiate → SubstituteTypeParam → ConditionalSelect`. Clients needing derivation-aware display walk the edges and present whichever chain is relevant.
   542	
   543	**Three distinct `OriginEdgeKind` taxonomies (do not conflate or reconcile).** The nine derivation kinds above live as `verter_session::semantic_query::OriginEdgeKind`. The audit substrate mirrors them and adds one audit-only kind: `verter_audit::OriginEdgeKind` = the same nine + `SharedLoadReuse` (emitted when a request joins a winner's in-flight artifact via scheduler dedup). The typeinfo **wire** graph uses a SEPARATE 10-arm graph-relationship taxonomy (proto `GraphOriginEdgeKind`: `DECLARES`/`INSTANTIATES`/`REFERENCES`/`MEMBER_OF`/`RESOLVES_TO`/`SHARED_LOAD_REUSE`/`FALLTHROUGH`/`RELATION_PROOF_STEP`/`BACK_EDGE_CYCLE`/`AUGMENTATION_STITCH`) — NOT the derivation taxonomy renamed, and only session↔audit is name-isomorphic (modulo `SharedLoadReuse`). The three lists are pinned by `origin_edge_taxonomy_locked` (`crates/verter_session/tests/cases/g_block/typeinfo_graph_contract_guards.rs`).
   544	
   545	**Typeinfo wire-contract guard surface.** The closed typeinfo wire surface (proto node/symbol/origin/request/error taxonomies, the split env-hash query identity, the closure-bound and schema-version request contracts, and the `AuditedResult` audit carrier) is pinned by a family of static guards under `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/g_block/typeinfo_{wire_surface,graph_contract,request_contract,audit_contract}_guards.rs`, all registered under the `Typeinfo Wire Contract` rule in `CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS`.
   546	
   547	**First-class telemetry.** `SemanticGraphStore` exposes `SemanticGraphStats` as a public API. Per-`SemanticQueryKey`-variant counters (cache hits, misses, same-path-sentinel returns, in-flight peak, cross-thread-join wait time) and per-dispatch-builder counters (instantiations, conditional branch selections, budget/fallback invocations, path length p50/p95, projection depth p50/p95, origin edges emitted, origin edges per node p50/p95) are mandatory — not an optional observability pass. The trace-check harness, benchmark pipeline, and feedback-file report at track exit consume `SemanticGraphStats::snapshot()` directly.
   548	
   549	## Worked Examples
   550	
   551	Normative fixtures. Any solver / dispatch change that breaks an expected behaviour below breaks the contract.
   552	
   553	### Example A — basic conditional
   554	
   555	```ts
   556	type MyType<T> = T extends string ? StringType : NotStringType;
   557	```
   558	
   559	- **Navigate(`MyType`)**: decl identity, parameters `[T]`, body shape `Conditional(check=T, extends=string)`. Do NOT descend into `StringType` / `NotStringType`. Stop at the open conditional shell.
   560	- **Expand(`MyType`)** (T unbound): return a `Conditional` graph with both branches materialized. Shape retains `T`, `string`, `StringType`, `NotStringType`. Origin layer carries `Instantiate(MyType, [T])` and structural links into each branch.
   561	- **Expand(`MyType<string>`)**: conditional is closed. Return only `StringType`. Origin layer carries `Instantiate(MyType, [string])`, `SubstituteTypeParam(T -> string)`, `ConditionalSelect(check=string extends string, branch=True)`. `NotStringType` is NOT walked and does NOT appear in the result.
   562	
   563	### Example B — intersection with mixed static and generic members
   564	
   565	```ts
   566	type Foo = { foo: number };
   567	type StringType = { a: Foo };
   568	type NotStringType = { a: Foo[] };
   569	type OtherType<T> = { a: Foo, b: T } & (T extends string ? StringType : NotStringType);
   570	```
   571	
   572	- **Navigate(`OtherType`)**: decl identity, parameters `[T]`, intersection shell with two arms: object `{ a, b }` and conditional `(T extends string ? … : …)`. Members `a` and `b` visible; `b` marked as a generic-parameter reference. Conditional arm stays a symbolic shell.
   573	- **Expand(`OtherType`)** (T unbound): object arm expands — `a: Foo` fully resolved, `b: T` preserves `T` as a parameter reference (origin links to the `[T]` parameter list). Conditional arm stays `Conditional` with both branches materialized. Intersection is NOT collapsed because the conditional remains open.
   574	- **Expand(`OtherType<string>`)**: object arm expands — `a: Foo`, `b: string` with `SubstituteTypeParam(T -> string)` origin. Conditional arm closes to `StringType`, which expands to `{ a: Foo }`. Intersection collapses to `{ a: Foo, b: string } & { a: Foo }` and normalizes; origin records `Normalize` over both contributing members.
   575	
   576	### Example C — `infer` inside a decidable conditional
   577	
   578	```ts
   579	type Foo = { a: number };
   580	type OtherFoo = Foo extends { a: infer T } ? T : never;
   581	```
   582	
   583	- The conditional is closed: `Foo` is concrete, `{ a: infer T }` is the extends pattern, no free parameters surround the check.
   584	- **Expand(`OtherFoo`)**: the relation engine matches `Foo` against `{ a: infer T }`, binds `T = number` via `InferBind`, selects the True branch, returns `number`. Origin: `ConditionalSelect(True)` + `InferBind(T = number)`.
   585	- **Navigate(`OtherFoo`)** follows the same reduction because `Navigate` reduces closed conditionals. The navigate result is the same `number` node. `infer` does NOT force a stop.
   586	
   587	### Example D — path-precise projection
   588	
   589	```ts
   590	type Foo = { foo: number };
   591	type StringType = { a: Foo };
   592	type NotStringType = { a: Foo };
   593	type OtherType<T> = { a: Foo, b: T } & (T extends string ? StringType : NotStringType);
   594	```
   595	
   596	- **`OtherType['a']['foo']`** (T unbound): project path `['a', 'foo']` through the intersection.
   597	  - Object arm contributes `a: Foo`; project `Foo['foo']` → `number`.
   598	  - Conditional arm is open; distribute `['a', 'foo']` into both branches.
   599	    - True: `StringType['a']['foo']` → `Foo['foo']` → `number`.
   600	    - False: `NotStringType['a']['foo']` → `Foo['foo']` → `number`.

   602	- **`OtherType<string>['a']['foo']`**: conditional is closed.
   603	  - Object arm: `Foo['foo']` → `number`.
   604	  - Conditional arm: `StringType['a']['foo']` → `number`. `NotStringType` is NEVER touched.
   605	  - Intersection collapses to `number`.
   606	
   607	This is path-precise projection, not whole-branch expansion. Sibling members and unrelated branches are not materialized.
   608	
   609	### Example E — nested open conditionals
   610	
   611	```ts
   612	type Deep<T> =
   613	  T extends string
   614	    ? (T extends "ab" | "cd" ? { kind: "pair"; value: T } : { kind: "str"; value: T })
   615	    : { kind: "other"; value: T };
   616	```
   617	
   618	- **Expand(`Deep`)** (T unbound): outer check is open. Keep outer `Conditional` shell. In the True branch, inner check is also open; keep inner `Conditional` shell. In the False branch, materialize `{ kind: "other"; value: T }` with `T` preserved.
   619	- **Expand(`Deep<"ab">`)**: outer check `"ab" extends string` closed → True. Inner check `"ab" extends "ab" | "cd"` closed → True. Return `{ kind: "pair"; value: "ab" }`. Origin chain: `Instantiate(Deep, ["ab"])` → `SubstituteTypeParam(T -> "ab")` → `ConditionalSelect(outer=True)` → `ConditionalSelect(inner=True)`.
   620	- **Expand(`Deep<"xx">`)**: outer closed → True. Inner `"xx" extends "ab" | "cd"` closed → False. Return `{ kind: "str"; value: "xx" }`. Origin: same outer chain, `ConditionalSelect(inner=False)`.
   621	
   622	> Template-literal pattern matching (e.g. `T extends \`${infer _}${infer _}\``) is a future relation-engine extension and is **not** part of this contract's normative fixtures. The nested-conditional semantics above apply uniformly once template-literal infer support lands — adding it does not require a contract revision.
   623	
   624	### Example F — contributors-only union / intersection combining
   625	
   626	```ts
   627	type A = { a: number; x: string };
   628	type B = { a: string; y: boolean };
   629	type C = { z: number };
   630	type AB = A | B | C;
   631	```
   632	
   633	- **`AB['a']`** projection: `A` contributes `number`, `B` contributes `string`, `C` does NOT contribute (no `a`). For a union, every member must contribute to the path; `C`'s miss makes the union projection a miss as a whole. (Contrast: if `AB` were `A | B` only, the result would be `number | string`.)
   634	- For intersection analogs (`A & B & C`): `A` contributes `number`, `B` contributes `string`, `C` does not contribute. Contributing arms' projection: `number & string` → `never` via intersection normalization. `C` is ignored for the path; the `never` arises from the contributors' intersection semantics, not from `C` being rewritten.
   635	
   636	## Shallow File State and Frontier Engine
   637	
   638	Cross-file type resolution for macros (`defineProps<T>()`, component-meta, etc.) is built on two shared primitives in `verter_session::resolver_core`:
   639	
   640	**ShallowFileState** (`shallow_file_state.rs`) is the authoritative shallow symbol/export surface for one imported type file. Keyed by `(canonical_id, whole_hash)`. Contains:
   641	- `exports` map (exported name -> `ExportTarget`: Local or Reexport)
   642	- `wildcard_reexports` (`export * from` sources, in declaration order)
   643	- `symbols` (all locally-declared type symbols with raw body, type params, local deps, external deps)
   644	- `import_locals` / `import_targets` (import classification for closure)
   645	
   646	Populated once through the shared host ensure-path and cached in `FileArtifactStore`. Invalidated when the file's whole-hash changes.
   647	
   648	**ExternalTypeFrontier** (`external_type_frontier.rs`) is the single BFS engine for all cross-file type deepening. Level-by-level traversal:
   649	1. Seed with initial `(canonical_id, exported_name)` pairs
   650	2. For each pending symbol: load `ShallowFileState` via `FrontierHost` trait, route the export (direct > alias > wildcard in declared order), run local closure
   651	3. Collect `ExternalSymbolRef` entries from unresolved external deps into the next level
   652	4. Dedup on `(canonical_id, exported_name)` across the entire request via `seen` set
   653	5. Repeat until frontier is empty or budget is exceeded
   654	
   655	**Barrel BFS contract:** when a pending file is a barrel and the requested symbol is not found in that file's shallow surface, process that file's wildcard barrel children as one BFS layer. Shallow every child in the layer before choosing any deeper barrel grandchildren. A barrel child that does not expose the requested symbol at its own shallow surface may contribute its wildcard children to the next layer, but must not trigger immediate depth-first descent.
   656	
   657	**Local closure** (`ShallowFileState::local_closure()`) resolves same-file transitive deps iteratively. Uses a visited set for cycle handling (revisited nodes silently skipped). Never crosses import boundaries -- external deps become `ExternalSymbolRef` for the frontier.
   658	
   659	**Budget contract** -- three domains with high ceilings (safety rails, not normal control flow):
   660	- `local_closure_steps`: 500 (same-file symbols per closure)
   661	- `frontier_symbol_visits`: 2000 (cross-file `(canonical_id, exported_name)` pairs)
   662	- `builder_expansion_steps`: 5000 (symbolic expansion steps)
   663	
   664	When a budget trips, the system returns a structured `BudgetExceededFailure` with domain, limit, actual count, and context -- never silently normalizes.
   665	
   666	**Host integration:** production route resolution enters through the
   667	request-bound `ResolverContext`. `ImportedRootDb` is the sole routed-target
   668	authority; `RouteDb` and current `IndexedReady` shallow facts resolve direct,
   669	named-reexport, and wildcard-barrel hops. Terminal semantic projection starts
   670	from that routed declaration and executes through `ProjectSemanticDispatch`.
   671	There is no host adapter that expands parser elements and no second frontier
   672	after `ImportedRootDb` selects the target.
   673	
   674	**Key files:**
   675	
   676	| File | Purpose |
   677	| --- | --- |
   678	| `crates/verter_session/src/resolver_core/shallow_file_state.rs` | ShallowFileState, ExportTarget, ShallowTypeSymbol, ExternalSymbolRef, ResolutionBudgets, local_closure() |
   679	| `crates/verter_session/src/resolver_core/external_type_frontier.rs` | ExternalTypeFrontier, FrontierHost trait, PendingExternalSymbol, ResolvedSymbol, RouteKind |
   680	| `crates/verter_session/src/host_resolve/external_type_resolution.rs` | Routed component-meta declaration and native projection entry points |
   681	| `crates/verter_session/src/host_resolve/frontier_engine.rs` | Named-export routing and route/index fact production |
   682	| `crates/verter_session/src/frontier_tests.rs` | Behavioral invariant tests (diamond dedup, barrel ordering, cycle termination, budget enforcement, etc.) |
   683	
   684	## Semantic Dispatch (current authority)
   685	
   686	**Architectural decision:** `ProjectSemanticDispatch` +
   687	`SemanticGraphStore` are the canonical lazy semantic layer and the sole
   688	authority for every reusable type-resolution operation. The
   689	`verter_semantic::analysis::type_solver` namespace now contains shared data
   690	carriers only; its former solve, relation, and projection execution modules are
   691	deleted.
   692	
   693	The reusable semantic layer lives in
   694	`crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/`. Each sub-module owns
   695	a distinct responsibility:
   696	
   697	- `mod.rs` — `ProjectSemanticDispatch` struct + `SemanticQueryApi::execute` impl
   698	- `build.rs` — `build_instantiate`, `build_mapped_type`,
   699	  `build_conditional`, `build_key_of`, `build_project_path`,
   700	  `build_typeof`, `build_builtin_utility`
   701	- `walk.rs` — `PathWalker` + `walk_path` (iterative worklist per plan §2)
   702	- `guards.rs` — `SubstitutionGuard`, `EvaluationGuard`, `WalkGuard`, `KeyEnumerationGuard`, `RelationGuard` (per-call RAII cycle detection)
   703	- `enumerate.rs` — `KeyEnumeration`, `EnumeratedKey`, `key_names_*` helpers
   704	- `relation.rs` — the SOLE relation authority (`execute_relate` riding `execute(SemanticQueryKey::Relate)`): reentry/assumption frames, coinductive SCC discharge, inference sessions, the O(tag) prefilter, and the structural reducer; `relation_txn.rs` carries the transient `CheckerTransaction` substrate
   705	- `lower.rs` — `shallow_lower_type_expr` (TypeExpr → `SemanticNodeId`); decl-body lowering is carrier-preserving under `Shallow` / `Navigate` / `Skeleton` (see Query Mode Contract)
   706	- `substitute.rs` — `substitute_semantic_type_param` (guarded)
   707	- `evaluate.rs` — `evaluate_deferred_semantic_node` (guarded)
   708	- `origin.rs` — origin-edge emitters
   709	
   710	**Class surfaces (`ResolveClassSurface` / `ResolveOverloadSet`).** A class resolves through two composed surfaces on the shared dispatch: the INSTANCE side (own members ∪ type-side heritage with dual-space substitution composition, visibility carried, `#private` excluded from the published keyspace) and the STATIC side (the `typeof C` constructor-object: own statics + own construct signature from the producer's `ValueDeclInfo.object_shape` — statics ride INSIDE that ObjectExpr, never a separate field — plus base statics composed via the type-side heritage refs, own-shadows-base precedence; a ctor-less subclass inherits the base ctor params with the derived instance return). `prototype` is synthesized at projection time as an instance-side `DeclRef`, never stored. Utility arms select by signature-kind BUCKET: `Parameters`/`ReturnType` read the call bucket, `ConstructorParameters`/`InstanceType` the construct bucket; class-ref payloads obtain the bucket via `ResolveClassSurface(Static)`; a bare-generic `ReturnType` instantiates at `unknown`. `ResolveOverloadSet` is a LIVE producer (`build_resolve_overload_set`): it settles the callee through the ONE shared signature-source carrier rail (`resolve_signature_source_carrier`, the same demand point the signature utilities use; the rails share the FUNCTION, not the CONTEXT — the utilities pass their caller's context while this key, being mode-erased, always settles under the non-published `StructuralTransit` context — and a `DeclRef`/`InstantiationRef` carrier callee still settles to the same signature group on both rails because `Instantiate` of a signature-bearing decl is mode-stable) and produces the ordered VISIBLE signature group — call bucket first, then construct — as the `OverloadSet(Arc<[SignatureRef]>)` value domain (the boundary `execute` wrap converts the group-bearing node; `execute_type_node` reports `ValueDomainMismatch` instead of leaking it as a type node). Visibility is `build_typeof`'s rule applied where the callee node was produced (a lone signature is visible even if bodied; a multi-signature group hides the trailing implementation), so the set's LAST element is the last visible overload — the signature-utility selection rule. Explicit `type_args` instantiate per candidate (non-accepting candidates drop; all-dropped ⇒ honest `Miss`); a signature-less callee is an honest `Miss`, never an empty set. `typeof C.make<string>` instantiation-expression args lower onto `ValueRef.type_args` and instantiate the resolved node at the typeof hop. Decorators never rewrite a surface — projection ignores them. Heritage hops run at the caller's demand (shallow-by-default); the facts rail records one `FileWholeHash` per heritage contributor.
   711	
   712	**Builtin settlement in `build_builtin_utility`.** `NonNullable<T>` is implemented: a settled union filters its nullish arms (an emptied union ⇒ `never`), settled non-nullable shapes pass through unchanged, nullish primitives reduce to `never`, and an UNSETTLED operand keeps the deferred `Opaque(Miss)` shell. `Awaited` remains deferred. (Note: `NonNullable` still makes NO closed-KEY-domain claim for the L1 key-domain predicate — value-producing utilities stay conservatively not-provably-closed there.)
   713	
   714	`SemanticGraphStore` (crate `verter_session::semantic_query_memo`) owns all reusable semantic identity via two parallel memos:
   715	
   716	- **Node memo** — mode-erased `FamilyKey` → `FamilySlots` map for single-node queries (`ResolveDecl`, `Instantiate`, `KeyOf`, `MappedType`, `Conditional`, `ProjectPath`, `TypeOf`, `NormalizeUnion`, `NormalizeIntersection`, `ResolvedNamedType`).
   717	- **Relation memo** — keyed by the full-identity `RelateMemoKey` (source / target / relation kind / policy / source freshness / inference context / env+substitution+projection-reduction context) for `Relate` judgements. Admission is decided-only: only the binary `Assignable { bindings }` / `NotAssignable` payloads publish (cache-with-fence); `Unknown`, `BudgetExceeded` (public payload, `cache_suppress`), session-local inference deltas, and abandoned sessions publish NOTHING — no memo entry, no fact signature, no reverse index.
   718	
   719	### Object-literal spreads: canonical construction programs
   720	
   721	Every spread-bearing object is a `SemanticNodeData::ObjectSpreadProgram(ObjectSpreadProgram)` — one immutable, source-ordered effect list (`DirectProperty` / `DirectMethod` / `DirectGet` / `DirectSet` / `DirectIndex` / `DirectCall` / `DirectConstruct` / `Spread`). It is the sole stored description of the object: no folded member surface, completeness mirror, replay cursor, or side log coexists. A non-spread object stays a closed `SemanticNodeData::Object` surface (every `SurfaceView` is closed by construction; the open-operand representation is gone). Direct effects carry lossless typed facts: typed key or computed-key child, value/signature children, optional/readonly, method/get/set kind, implementation-body fact, visibility, spans/declaration origin, and excess origin.
   722	
   723	Typed property keys flow end to end: `PropertyKey = String | Number(CanonicalIndexInt) | UniqueSymbol(DeclIdentity)`, and `AuthoredPropertyKey = Known(..) | Computed(child)`. Identifier/string-literal equivalence is centralized; numeric keys use the checked canonical-index rules; unique symbols compare by nominal declaration identity, never display spelling; unresolved computed keys stay typed children (they are never stringified). Element access coerces a numeric key and its canonical string spelling; `keyof` keeps the authored variant. A `#private` class brand is not a type-level member.
   724	
   725	`ExcessPropertyOrigin` still participates in canonical node identity (`Eq` / `Hash`), not request-local metadata. Direct literal writes are `FreshOwn`; spread-introduced or spread-overlapped members are `SpreadTainted`; all other origins are `NonLiteral`.
   726	
   727	The fresh excess-property prepass is a dormant engine capability. No production caller constructs a relation ask with `excess_property_check: true`; non-test policy and oracle plumbing default the flag to `false`. Direct relation-level tests exercise the capability, but only a future production caller explicitly setting `excess_property_check: true` on a fresh-source relation activates it in production.
   728	
   729	**One correlated projection family.** `SemanticQueryKey::ProjectObjectSpread { program, selector, context }` evaluates programs. Selectors: `Key`, `RelationShape`, `Surface`, `IndexDomain`, `Signature`, `EnumerableValueEnvelope`, `ExcessEligibility`. The sealed dispatch-constructed context carries the projection-reduction axes, the R/T/L/J environment hashes, the substitution identity, and the exact-optional-property policy; prepared and family identity include all of them, so distinct selectors/environments/views never cross-serve.
   730	
   731	Finite enumerable union operands fork whole alternatives at their exact spread position, and later effects apply per branch, so correlation survives overwrites. Selector liveness prunes only shadowed recursive effects before recursion (`Key(x)` on `{...Self, x}` never enters `Self`; `{x, ...Self}` must). An alternative's public surface is positive evidence only: omission never proves absence, emptiness, exact `keyof`, exhaustive domain, or closed materialization. Those operations exist only on the sealed witnesses `ClosedObjectProjectionAlternative` / `ClosedObjectProjectionFormula`; an open or mixed formula cannot mint one.
   732	
   733	Optional spread writes fold per branch: absent + optional → optional right-present value; required/optional left + optional → required/optional union of presents; a live open residual keeps presence but makes value/facets indeterminate; a later required direct write restores exactness. The exact-optional policy controls authored `undefined` (`1|2` vs `1|2|undefined`), and environments never cross-hit. Spread-copied index facts lose readonly; authored direct indices keep it. An index constrains values when a key exists but never manufactures named presence. Direct call/construct effects survive in distinct buckets; a callable/constructable operand contributes neither.
   734	
   735	**Excess eligibility is a whole-program selector**: `Eligible { direct_candidates }`, `SuppressedByGenericSpread`, or `Indeterminate`. Any semantically generic spread suppresses all direct candidates before or after it (even under a finite-looking constraint); closed/enumerable spreads do not suppress and spread-provided keys are never candidates; operational inability to classify a residual is `Indeterminate`, which falls back safely (no rejection). Generic-to-concrete substitution re-evaluates eligibility. The prepass consumes programs through this selector and requires closed alternatives for absence.
   736	
   737	**Relation consumes correlated alternatives with exact quantifiers**: every source alternative must assign to some target alternative; reject only with complete negative proof; open/indeterminate evidence falls back to `Unknown`. Program roots are recognized before self-equality, shortcuts, inference deposits, excess, `Record`, index, and signature loops. `{...T} <= {...T}` stays non-publishing `Unknown` while `T` is unresolved, despite identical node ids. Required named target keys need named required presence — a source index never satisfies it. Broad `Record`/index obligations relate every known contribution and require an exact envelope per live residual; open targets reject on exact known mismatches before closure but stay `Unknown` on a passing known subset. Inference deposits only from exact whole-branch positions inside the existing transaction checkpoints — indeterminate positions deposit nothing. Alternative-product caps, depth caps, and recursive breaks are typed operational partials (`BudgetExceeded` / recursive), ReturnOnly and admitted nowhere; a later adequate run heals. Cross-thread owner wait-cycles break with a typed recursive partial under the store's owner wait-for graph.
   738	
   739	Raising/display preserves exact effect order when no closed formula exists (never spreads-first); the shallow typeinfo surface joins positive members with `members_complete = false` unless a single closed alternative proves the domain. On the wire, `GraphObjectSpreadProgram` (tag 33) carries the ordered lossless effect list under graph schema 7.
   740	
   741	**Known debt.**
   742	
   743	- *Consumer projection context carries an empty substitution (G-m1).* `project_object_spread_for_consumer` builds the sealed query context with `SubstitutionCanonicalHash::empty()`. Query identity still includes that context, so no cross-serving occurs, but a caller that genuinely runs under a substitution gets the empty-substitution answer; threading the live substitution through the context factory remains open. (The optionality half is CLOSED: `ExactOptionalPropertyPolicy` is threaded from `relation_strict_config().exact_optional_property_types` — the `strict_family_relax_bits` host knob, bit `0b100` — and pinned by `exact_optional_property_types_threads_into_consumer_projections`.)
   744	
   745	**Canonical deferred forms** (plan §2 — only these variants cross any cache boundary):
   746	
   747	- `SemanticNodeData::Mapped { source, mapper }` — deferred mapped type
   748	- `SemanticNodeData::Conditional { check, extends, true_branch_ref, false_branch_ref, distributive }` — deferred conditional
   749	- `SemanticNodeData::IndexedAccess { object, index }` — deferred indexed access
   750	- `SemanticNodeData::KeyOf { base }` — deferred keyof
   751	- `SemanticNodeData::TypeOf(carrier::TypeOfCarrier)` — deferred typeof (opaque payload; head fields `value_root`/`path` via `typeof_head`, args via `carrier_type_args`, rebuild via `map_carrier_type_args`)
   752	- `SemanticNodeData::TypeParam { name }` — open type parameter reference
   753	- `SemanticNodeData::Alias(target)` — alias identity preservation (target must be `DeclAnchor`-identifiable — plan Change B)
   754	- `SemanticNodeData::Opaque(err)` — genuine projection miss or structured budget failure
   755	- `SemanticNodeData::Signature { kind: SignatureKind::{Call,Construct}, params, return_type, type_parameters }` — the ONE signature shape for call (`(…) => R`) and construct (`new (…) => R`) signatures; kind participates in node identity, `Call` raises to `TypeExpr::Function` and `Construct` to `TypeExpr::ConstructorType`; class/interface lower to `Object` with heritage merged (a class's construct bucket holds `Signature(Construct)` nodes)
   756	- `SemanticNodeData::Infer { name }` vs `SemanticNodeData::InferRef { name }` — representation INVARIANT: an infer DECLARATION (`Infer`, the literal `infer X` binder in a conditional's `extends` pattern) and an infer REFERENCE (`InferRef`, a use of the bound name — e.g. a true-branch `X`) are DISTINCT node kinds and must never intern identically. The distinction is load-bearing for capture-avoidance: the conditional substitution arm's shadow stop keys on a literal `Infer` DECLARATION in a nested conditional's own `extends` pattern, so collapsing references onto the declaration node would either capture a genuine re-bind or drop a legitimate outer substitution. The literal `infer X` syntax is the ONLY producer of an `Infer` node; name bindings hand out `InferRef` nodes.
   757	
   758	All surrogate encodings are retired: `Alias(KeyOf(source))` (replaced by canonical `Mapped` shell with `KeyEnumeration::Unresolvable` branch), arena `Node::Error { description }` used as a materialisation sentinel, `Primitive(Undefined)` returned from failed solver projections.
   759	
   760	**No SILENT semantic-complexity caps in the semantic layer.** A hard-coded step/depth cap used as a SEMANTIC budget — one that silently truncates a resolution and hands back a bare node a consumer classifies as settled — is forbidden. Three legacy silent caps were deleted or reclassified:
   761	
   762	- `evaluate_deferred_semantic_node`'s `for _ in 0..32` — DELETED; replaced by stack-local `EvaluationGuard` cycle detection.
   763	- `PathWalker::max_depth = 64` — DELETED; replaced by `WalkGuard` cycle detection.
   764	- Parser-level `MAX_TYPE_RESOLUTION_DEPTH = 64` — RENAMED to `PARSER_SYNTACTIC_DEPTH_LIMIT = 256` and documented as syntactic stack-safety, not a semantic budget.
   765	
   766	**Retained runaway-safety fuses (distinct from — not a contradiction of — the above).** Two hard fuses REMAIN and are correct precisely because visited-node cycle detection cannot bound FRESH-NODE regrowth (each operator re-dispatch / `Instantiate` step can mint a brand-new node id the `visited` set has never seen, so a cycle set alone does not terminate a runaway): the deferred evaluator's recursion ceiling `EVALUATE_DEFERRED_DEPTH_CEILING = 256` (stack safety) and the residual-carrier demand step fuse `STRUCTURAL_FACT_DEMAND_FUSE = 64` (backing `normalize_node_for_structural_fact_demand` / `peel_node_for_uninstantiated_carrier_fact_demand` and `resolve_signature_source_carrier`). Neither is a silent semantic cap: a trip returns a TYPED `ResultCompleteness::Partial` (`DEFERRED_EVALUATION_LIMIT` / `STRUCTURAL_FACT_DEMAND_LIMIT`) — node-HIDING at the demand surface (`StructuralFactDemandOutcome::Partial` carries no `SemanticNodeId`), never warm-admitted (`ComputeAdmission::ReturnOnly`), and folded into the enclosing build's taint frame (`into_active_query_build_node` → `fold_local_partial_completeness`) so no consumer can ever classify a truncated carrier as a settled result.
   767	
   768	**Bounded-loop annotation convention.** Any bounded loop in `crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/` MUST be annotated `// bounded-loop: <reason>` on the preceding line. Approved reasons: `fence-retry` (CLAUDE.md completion-fence 3-retry rule); and a runaway-safety fuse / `visited`-set cycle stop that returns a TYPED `Partial` and is never warm-admitted (the residual-carrier step fuse in the structural-fact demand loop and `resolve_signature_source_carrier`, plus the annotated `visited`/fuse loops in `build.rs` / `relation.rs` / `absorb.rs` / `walk.rs`). A bare numeric cap with no typed-`Partial` exit is NOT an approved reason.
   769	
   770	**Recursion guard contract.** Per-call `in_flight: FxHashSet<SemanticNodeId>` + RAII pop + completion memo. Stack-local; dies with the call; NOT a host-owned cache:
   771	
   772	| Function | Cycle sentinel | Publishable | Publication surface |
   773	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
   774	| `substitute_semantic_type_param` | input node unchanged | yes | Caller's `SemanticQueryKey` memo |
   775	| `evaluate_deferred_semantic_node` | current node (fix-point) | yes | Caller's `SemanticQueryKey` memo |
   776	| `walk_path` | `Opaque(QueryError::AliasCycle { chain })` | yes | Originating `ProjectPath` memo |
   777	| `key_names_from_base_node` / `_keyspace_node` | `KeyEnumeration::Unresolvable` | no (Rust-local) | Caller publishes canonical `Mapped` shell |
   778	| `execute_relate` | scoped `RelationStep::Assumed` (coinductive assumption on the per-transaction reentry stack) | never (the sentinel is never admitted; a discharged SCC publishes `Assignable`/`NotAssignable`, `Unknown` is ReturnOnly-only) | `Relate` family slot (decided binary payloads only) |
   779	
   780	**Parser → semantic graph integration.** Parser output is syntax-only route
   781	inventory. `route_inventory.rs` records authored imports, exports, reexports,
   782	and export assignments. From the same retained program and exact owner table,
   783	semantic `ScriptShallowIndex` pairs those routes with `DeclHeaderIndex`, while
   784	semantic `decl_dependencies` produces per-declaration dependency names on
   785	demand. The indexed lowering service converts authored declaration bodies into
   786	owned typed IR on demand; semantic queries then enter
   787	`ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute`. No parser cache adapter stores or returns
   788	resolved type surfaces.
   789	
   790	**Authority-uniqueness contract** (normative, mechanically enforced by §6.5 gate tests):
   791	
   792	- A second `impl SemanticQueryApi for ...` — FORBIDDEN (besides `ProjectSemanticDispatch`).
   793	- A second relation entry point — FORBIDDEN (`execute_relate` in `project_semantic_dispatch::relation` is the sole authority; a bare-pair `relate_nodes` may not return).
   794	- A second `fn shallow_lower_type_expr` — FORBIDDEN (besides `project_semantic_dispatch::lower`).
   795	- A second struct owning a `RelationMemo` field — FORBIDDEN (besides `SemanticGraphStore`).
   796	- A second struct owning the semantic node map — FORBIDDEN (besides `SemanticGraphStore`).

   820	project the resulting semantic graph only at their output boundary.
