   822	## Declaration symbol inventories
   823	
   824	`verter_semantic::analysis::type_eval` contains the shallow per-file
   825	declaration inventory. `EvalEnv` stores content-free facts and authored-body
   826	locators for ordered type/value contributor groups and augmentation scopes. It
   827	stores no `TypeExpr` and performs no evaluation. Authored bodies are lowered
   828	on demand by the shared semantic dispatch.
   829	
   830	The parser's `route_inventory` module owns authored syntax routes only. The
   831	semantic `ScriptShallowIndex` joins those routes with declaration headers, and
   832	semantic `decl_dependencies` owns structural dependency names. These layers
   833	perform no type evaluation and expose no resolved-element carrier. Query-time
   834	finite types are governed by the shared semantic-dispatch contract above.
   835	
   836	## Declaration Merging (CRITICAL)
   837	
   838	Same-name TypeScript declaration merging is owned end-to-end by the shared layer; there is exactly ONE merge path.
   839	
   840	**Carrier chain (owner → reducer):**
   841	
   842	- `EvalEnv.type_symbols`/`value_symbols` are `FxHashMap<String, TypeDeclGroup>`/`ValueDeclGroup` — ordered contributor groups. `add_type`/`add_value` APPEND (`group.contributors.push`), never last-wins `insert`. `TypeDeclGroup::merged_body()` returns `TypeDeclBody::Merged { contributors, kinds }` for any ≥2-contributor group whose contributors are ALL `interface` or `class` (`interface`+`interface` AND `interface`+`class` fold — the interface members augment the class INSTANCE type; the class value/static/constructor side stays on a separate value declaration). Every other group — a single contributor, or any group containing a type `alias` (a duplicate-identifier error in TS) — returns `TypeDeclBody::Single` (the last-wins representative). `ValueDeclGroup::merged_signatures()` concatenates every contributor's signatures in source order.
   843	- `ShallowTypeSymbol` / `ShallowValueSymbol` are SLIM HEADER views — they OWN no body product and hold NO `Arc<Lowered*Decl>` handle. `ShallowTypeSymbol` carries header facts only (`kind`, `type_param_names`, `member_names`, `contributor_count`); `ShallowValueSymbol` carries `kind`, `object_member_headers`, and the `.vue`-default provenance flag `is_synthesised_vue_default`. They are built directly from the `DeclHeaderIndex` (no body lowering), so `ShallowFileState::symbol(name)` / `value_symbol(name)` are header-only probes. The THREE demand surfaces are separate accessors on `ShallowFileState`: **body** — `type_decl(name) -> Arc<LoweredTypeDecl>` / `value_decl(name) -> Arc<LoweredValueDecl>` (the single `DeclBodyMemo`-owned lowered result, lowered on first touch; `value_decl` routes synthesised `.vue`-default bodies first); **dependency edges** — `type_deps(name) -> Arc<ClassifiedTypeDeps>` (per-state `local_deps` / `external_deps`, cached, edges ONLY — never a body); **augmentation bodies** — `augmentation_type_decl(scope, name)` / `augmentation_value_decl(scope, name)`. The synthesised `.vue`-default is an eager macro-producer `LoweredValueDecl` stored in a dedicated body map (read through `value_decl`), with its slim header in `synthesised_value_symbols`. Shallow same-file member readers consult the content-free body surface — `type_decl(name)` yields `LoweredTypeDecl` whose `body` is `TypeDeclBody` (`Single`/`Merged` contributor SLOTS only; no `lookup_object` / embedded `TypeExpr` on the prepare surface). Member-name inventory comes from the slim header (`member_names` / `DeclHeaderIndex`); typed body demand re-borrows authored bounds lease-only through the shared lazy lowering path and reduces on the graph, never via a prepare-surface object projection. `PreparedTypeDecl` records merged declarations as `body_facts.merged_contributor_slots: Arc<[TypeBodySlot]>` (empty = single) — ordered content-free body-slot LOCATORS, never embedded `TypeExpr` bodies (the whole `PreparedTypeDecl` is fact+locator `NoTypeExpr`); the slim shallow symbols are thinner still (header facts only).
   844	- Body lowering (`lower_decl_body_with_provenance`) interns a merged interface as a distinct `SemanticNodeData::MergedDecl { contributors: Arc<[SemanticNodeId]> }` carrier; a single declaration lowers exactly as before.
   845	
   846	**The load-bearing rule:** a merged declaration MUST reach the reducer as `MergedDecl`. A bare `TypeExpr::Intersection`/`SemanticNodeData::Intersection` is FORBIDDEN as the merged-decl representation — the intersection reducer applies own-body-shadows-heritage member precedence and cannot accumulate method overload groups (a same-named method in a later arm SHADOWS the earlier). `verter_session` may route/consume contributors but MUST NOT synthesise the merge as `raw_body = TypeExpr::intersection(...)`.
   847	
   848	**Peer-merge reducer** (`reduce_merged_decl_with_graph` + `merge_declaration_surfaces`, in `project_semantic_dispatch::walk`; routed through raise / expand / keyof / relation / substitute): (a) same-name methods/call-signatures ACCUMULATE into one ordered overload group (member value = ordered `Intersection` of the per-contributor function nodes); (b) conflicting non-method properties take deterministic first-contributor precedence (never `never`); (c) distinct members union; call/construct/index signatures concatenate. **`extends`/`implements` heritage is PRESERVED:** each contributor is split into its own-body surface(s) and its heritage `Ref` arms (a contributor lowers to `Intersection([heritage Ref…, own Object])`); own bodies peer-merge, then the reducer re-emits `Intersection([heritage…, merged_own_Object])` so the existing heritage-overlay path resolves inherited members lazily (own members shadow inherited same-name members). Dropping the heritage arms would lose inherited members from a `interface X extends Base {…}` + `interface X {…}` merge.
   849	
   850	**One merge engine, two consumers — display is non-mutating.** The peer-merge precedence lives in a single pure helper `merge_declaration_surfaces_core` (member union + first-contributor precedence + ordered method-overload accumulation, NO interning, NO own-body-shadows-heritage branch — that shadowing is the intersection reducer's job over real heritage arms). `merge_declaration_surfaces` calls the core then interns the overload groups + `Object`; the `display()` projection (`reduce_merged_decl_display_surface`) calls the SAME core and renders the result WITHOUT interning, so rendering a `SemanticNodeData::MergedDecl` leaves `node_count` unchanged and is byte-identical to the canonical reduced surface (an accumulated overload renders as the property-intersection `m: (..) & (..)`, exactly as the reduced `Object` does — never as separate method signatures). Display must never call the interning reducer or dispatch (guard: `display_source_does_not_call_graph_interning_or_dispatch`).
   851	
   852	**Overload visibility** is a projection-time rule (`build_typeof`): a lone signature is visible (even if bodied); a multi-signature group surfaces every bodiless overload in source order and HIDES the trailing implementation (`has_implementation_body == true`).
   853	
   854	**Versioning:** same-file merged values root on the owner's single `FileWholeHash` self-root under a content-free query-identity key (R6) — no dedicated contributor-sequence fact. Cross-file ambient augmentation (`declare module`/`declare global`) is a separate concern documented under **Declaration Augmentation (CRITICAL)** below — it reuses this same `MergedDecl` peer-merge path, it is not a second merge engine.
   855	
   856	**Guards** (registered in `critical_rules_have_guards.rs::CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS`): `eval_env_type_symbols_are_grouped_not_last_wins_map`, `eval_env_add_decl_appends_not_overwrites`, `no_intersection_merge_synthesis_in_verter_session`, `merged_decl_lowers_to_distinct_carrier_not_intersection`, plus the discriminating `declaration_merge_facts` regression and the `declaration_merge` typeinfo oracles.
   857	
   858	**Merge/augmentation WIRE domain (architecture decision).** The wire representation of a merged declaration / module augmentation is ALREADY modelled inside `GraphTypeNode`: kinds **21–25** (`GraphMergedDeclaration` `{merged_symbol, repeated GraphDeclarationPart parts}`, `GraphAmbientModule`, `GraphModuleAugmentation`, `GraphAmbientNamespace`, `GraphGlobalAugmentation`), with decl anchors as nested `GraphDeclarationPart`. The LIVE carrier behind that wire surface is the graph node `SemanticNodeData::MergedDecl { contributors }` — reduced to an `Object` / overload surface and emitted as a `GraphTypeNode`. The `SemanticQueryValue::DeclarationAnalysis(DeclarationAnalysisValue)` value variant is a **non-live shell** with NO producer and is NOT the wire carrier (its rustdoc points back here). A proposal to relocate merge to a distinct `DeclarationAnalysisGraph` wire message is **rejected**: the correct home already exists in the closed contract, so adding the message would be dead duplicate surface (new tags + TS bindings + validation + a `schema_version` bump + permanent compat). A structured-merge-graph producer (actual `GraphMergedDeclaration` emission) lands ONLY together with its first real FFI/TS consumer, as the existing kind 21 — never as a separate message. Do not re-flag "missing wire-proto relocation" as an incomplete deliverable.
   859	
   860	## Declaration Augmentation (CRITICAL)
   861	
   862	Ambient declaration augmentation (`declare module "X" { ... }` / `declare global { ... }`) is a RETAINED, addressable scoped inventory — never fingerprint-only facts and never file-scope pollution.
   863	
   864	**Typed inventory (the single source of truth).** The binder retains every augmentation-block inner declaration on `EvalEnv`, keyed by `(AugmentationScopeKind {Global, Module(specifier)}, name)`:
   865	
   866	- `EvalEnv.augmentation_scopes` → ordered `TypeDeclGroup` (interfaces / type aliases), served by `ShallowFileState::augmentation_type_decl(scope, name)` as a demand-lowered `Arc<LoweredTypeDecl>` (the eager header inventory lists the scoped names; bodies lower through the memo on first touch).
   867	- `EvalEnv.augmentation_value_scopes` → ordered `ValueDeclGroup` (`const`/`let`/`var`, `function`, `class`), served by `ShallowFileState::augmentation_value_decl(scope, name)` as a demand-lowered `Arc<LoweredValueDecl>`.
   868	
   869	Inner declarations NEVER enter file-scope `type_symbols`/`value_symbols`. Parse-domain `ModuleAugmentationFact`s are DERIVED from this typed inventory (`fact_emission::collect_augmentations`) — one fact per `(scope, name)` carrying the augmented name, its symbol space, and a HEADER-level shape fingerprint (kind + syntactic member headers + contributor count): publish hashes no bodies (honoring the zero-body-lowering publish invariant), so the fingerprint is invariant under a member's VALUE-type edit. Body sensitivity for every augmentation consumer therefore rides the per-contributor `FileWholeHash` facts, which BOTH the semantic augmentation stitch (`project_semantic_dispatch::collect_augmentation_contributions`) AND the compile-tier augmentation rail (`compile_fact_emission::observe_augmentation_fingerprints`) record alongside the header-level `ModuleAugmentationIndexShape` fingerprint — a member-body edit moves the augmenter's whole-hash and invalidates the consumer on both rails. There is NO raw-source byte-scan (Build Philosophy: no stage rescans raw source to rediscover what shallow processing captured — guard `shallow_walk_invariant::fact_emission_reads_only_shallow_state_never_raw_source`). There is no `ScopeId.kind`/`semantic_query::ScopeKind` — the live addressing is `AugmentationScopeKind` alone.
   870	
   871	**Cross-file augmentation merge is the SAME `MergedDecl` peer-merge path as same-file merging — NOT a second merge engine.** When a declaration `(canonical, name)` is instantiated, `stitch_module_augmentations` (in `project_semantic_dispatch::build`) finds every augmenter file via `FileArtifactStore::ensure_augmentation_index_populated`, fetches each augmenter's RETAINED inner declaration from the memo-owned augmentation inventory (`ShallowFileState::augmentation_type_decl(scope, name)` / `augmentation_value_decl(scope, name)`; typed-IR only — never a source/byte scan in the resolver), lowers it in the augmenter's own file context through `prepare_augmentation_type_decl` + `lower_decl_body_with_provenance`, and folds base ∪ augmenter contributions into ONE `SemanticNodeData::MergedDecl` carrier (flattening the base body if it is already a `MergedDecl`). Augmenter order is the stable `(canonical, parse_stable_hash)` key — discovery-order-independent. Relative-augmenter discovery loads the base's `reverse_deps_for` before the index scan.
   872	
   873	**Overlay-aware index.** `AugmentationTargetKey.population: AugmentationPopulation {Base, Session(u64)}`. A `Base` scan reads `is_base()` artifacts only (base parse-env hash + current parser version); a `Session` scan reads the session's overlay artifacts (matched by the session overlay discriminator) UNIONED with base, keyed by the overlay-set fingerprint. **`Session(u64)` is the overlay-set fingerprint, NOT a raw session id** — the producer (the body stitch) and the route-surface validator (`HostStoreView::validates_route_surface_domain`) derive `(population, overlay_discriminator)` through the SINGLE shared `session_view::augmentation_population_for_view`, so a session view can never be cached as, or validated against, a base-only set. Overlay augmenters NEVER poison the base index and NEVER cross sessions. There is NO base-only `assert!(view.compat_token().session.is_none(), …)` on the augmentation-index surface — a session view is accepted under `Session` population.
   874	
   875	**Cross-file FACTS** ride the stitch's own rail: the cold stitch observes one `FactKey::ModuleAugmentationIndexShape` (the augmenter-set fingerprint — the SOLE `RouteSurface` fact) plus one `FileWholeHash` per contributing file (base ∪ augmenters), and records `self_root_canonicals = {base} ∪ {augmenters}`. A content edit to ANY contributor misses the warm read; torn/partial routes through `ReturnOnly`, never warmed. Query keys stay content-free (R6).
   876	
   877	**Guards** (registered in `critical_rules_have_guards.rs::CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS`): `session_overlay_augmenter_isolated_from_base_index`, `session_overlay_augmentation_isolated_from_base_meta` (the e2e overlay-isolation oracle).
   878	
   879	## Cross-File Type Resolution (Compiler Integration)
   880	
   881	Typed Vue macro semantics are projected by the host into compiler-facing DTOs:
   882	
   883	1. `produce_vue_macro_codegen` inventories one already-indexed SFC under one
   884	   request-bound resolver context.
   885	2. It resolves each typed macro root through `ProjectSemanticDispatch` and
   886	   independently produces runtime and/or terminal TSC entries.
   887	3. It returns `MacroRuntimeBundle` / `MacroTscBundle` entries keyed by stable
   888	   macro `syntax_index`, plus the exact transitive canonical footprint.
   889	4. The compiler consumes the explicit `VueMacroSemanticInput`; it never
   890	   resolves typed macro parameters or merges companion/external type maps.
   891	
   892	The producer output is request-local. Its aggregate bundle is not a durable
   893	cache; underlying semantic query nodes retain their normal memo and
   894	singleflight behavior. The Rust compiler performs no file I/O and is not a
   895	type-resolution authority.
   896	
   897	**Shallow file state and semantic-dispatch integration:**
   898	`ShallowFileState` (the shallow symbol/export surface per imported file,
   899	keyed by `(canonical_id, whole_hash)`) and `ExternalTypeFrontier` (the
   900	layered BFS route/dependency engine) are the shared cross-file discovery
   901	primitives. Local closure runs same-file dependencies iteratively without
   902	crossing import boundaries. The frontier records route and dependency facts;
   903	it does not evaluate a terminal type body. See
   904	`resolver_core/shallow_file_state.rs`,
   905	`resolver_core/external_type_frontier.rs`, `host_resolve/frontier_engine.rs`,
   906	and `resolver_core/imported_root_db.rs`.
   907	
   908	All query-time expansion for macro types, component-meta, and imported aliases
   909	enters through `ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute`. Consumer-specific framework
   910	surfaces and macro DTOs are terminal projections of the shared graph result.
   911	`type_eval.rs` is a content-free declaration inventory, and `type_solver/`
   912	contains retained DTOs only; neither is an execution engine.
   913	
   914	## Macro Type Traversal Rule
   915	
   916	When resolving cross-file macro types (`defineProps<T>()`, `defineEmits<T>()`, and other shared host-backed queries), only follow the import graph reachable from the requested type's declaration graph.
   917	
   918	**Macro resolution is one shared path — `shared_resolve(type) + normalise`.** Every macro (`defineProps` / `defineEmits` / `defineOptions` / `defineSlots` / `withDefaults`) and every imported `.vue` component surface resolves through exactly TWO steps:
   919	
   920	1. **Resolve ONE type via the shared resolver** — the generic-parameter type (`define*<T>()`) OR the object-argument type (`define*({ ... })`). `withDefaults` resolves the props payload type plus the defaults-object type and merges. `.vue`-component imports resolve the imported component's synthesized `$props` / `$emit` / `$slots` / expose surface recursively through the same dispatch (the hardest case — apply EXTRA caution: it is exactly where rule violations cause the worst hangs). Resolution is ALWAYS the shared typed-IR five-mode dispatch — no macro-specific engine, no per-surface walker, no eager element resolver.
   921	2. **Normalize from the stored stream (a thin transform, NOT a resolver)** — props: defaults / optionality / readonly / declaration provenance / `declared_in_macro_type_arg`; emits: walk the canonical `SurfaceEntry` stream once and expand each call-signature or property producer directly into a complete occurrence without a kind-array merge, name join, ordinal join, or post-hoc reorder; a resolved concrete property payload must be tuple/function-shaped, while an incompatible concrete payload closes the macro as `MacroInvalidReason::InvalidEmitsShape` on both Runtime and TSC demands (`{}` remains a valid empty emits surface, and open/opaque payloads retain conservative projection); the call-signature payload strips the leading event-name parameter; slots: function-like members only, first-parameter object becomes bindings, return type preserved; options/expose: pass-through object surface.
   922	
   923	A macro/import that resolves its surface through anything other than the shared resolver, or flattens a full surface eagerly before the consumer demands it, is a rule violation — collapse it into `shared_resolve(type) + normalise`.
   924	
   925	- There is one shared cross-file type resolver. Consumer-specific ownership rules live in `/component-meta`.
   926	- The resolver has exactly five query modes (see "Query Mode Contract" above):
   927	  - `Identity`: declaration identity and canonical source location only. No body read, no shape materialization.
   928	  - `Navigate`: minimum semantic work needed to continue a requested path. Intermediate hops run in this mode.
   929	  - `Shallow`: one surface level of the requested node without recursive expansion.
   930	  - `Expanded`: recursive materialization of the requested result.
   931	  - `Skeleton`: specialised generic-helper/cycle traversal that keeps unbound type parameters as shells.
   932	- `Skeleton` is a distinct mode, not a synonym for `Navigate`. It is currently scoped to cycle/generic-helper traversal — the materialization cycle gate's per-hop `Instantiate` (`ClassifyMaterializationCycleGate`, see `project_semantic_dispatch::cycle_gate`). New call sites must justify why they need Skeleton semantics instead of `Navigate` / `Shallow`.
   933	- Do not introduce ad hoc navigate/shallow flags; use the canonical modes and the path-precise projection surface.
   934	- Do not walk unrelated imports from the same file.
   935	- Do not treat plain imports as implicit exports.
   936	- Keep direct re-exports (`export { X } from`, `export * from`) as an explicit separate path.
   937	- Parsing a `.ts`/`.js`/declaration file for type resolution must cache discovered symbol name -> canonical location mappings.
   938	- Re-exported names and barrel hops must also be cached once discovered. If traversal follows `export * from './foo'`, cache that result so later lookups do not rescan the same barrel chain.
   939	
   940	If a file imports 20 modules but the requested macro type only references `AvatarProps` and `IconProps`, external resolution must only traverse those reachable dependencies.
   941	
   942	**TS-first resolution priority:** TypeScript types always take priority over JavaScript files when resolving ambiguous dependency candidates. Verter is a type-strict compiler that relies on TS typing for correctness. JS files should only be used as a last resort when no TS type definition is available. When `DependencyResolution.possible_canonical_ids` contains multiple candidates, use `effective_target()` which selects the single highest-priority candidate: `.d.ts` > `.d.cts` > `.d.mts` > `.ts` > `.tsx` > `.js` > `.jsx` > `.cjs` > `.mjs`. Do not try remaining candidates if the selected one lacks the needed type -- treat as not found.
   943	
   944	**Owned resolution is bounded by `workspace_root`:** For owned and project-scoped resolution, `node_modules` and package `#imports` ancestor walks stop at `IdeProjectConfig.workspace_root`. In monorepos, `workspace_root` may be above `project_root` to reach hoisted `node_modules`. In compat `createCheckerByJson()`, `workspace_root == project_root`. Unowned resolution (no owning project) remains unbounded. The boundary is passed via `ancestor_dirs(path, Some(&workspace_root))` and `ancestor_dirs_from_dir(start_dir, Some(&workspace_root))` in `verter_workspace::resolver`.
   945	
   946	## Typed-IR-Only Resolver Rule (CRITICAL)
   947	
   948	The native component-meta / typeinfo resolver pipeline drives every semantic decision from the typed IR (`TypeExpr` on the Rust side, `TypeDescriptor` from `@verter/type-ir` on the TS side). Source slicing, regex against type text, hand-rolled type-text splitters, `starts_with("Pick<")` shape sniffing, the synthesise-then-reparse pattern (`format!(...).parse_type_annotation(...)`), and `path.contains("/node_modules/")` classification are all forbidden inside that pipeline.
   949	
   950	- OXC AST lowers to `TypeExpr` via `lower_ts_type(ts_type, source)` (in `verter_semantic::analysis::type_expr_lower`) at exactly two boundary classes: macro / JSDoc PRODUCER fields lower eagerly at their producer boundary (stored on `Analyzed*Field`, `ResolvedLocalType.type_expr`, surviving every cache); top-level DECLARATION BODIES lower LAZILY on first semantic demand through the scheduler-retained parse snapshot (`DeclBodyMemo` → `DeclLoweringService`), NOT eagerly during shallow analysis — an `IndexedReady` publish lowers ZERO declaration bodies. Either way the analyzer/lowering arm takes an OXC node it already holds; downstream stages walk the resulting `TypeExpr`, never re-parse or re-lower at query time.
   951	- `parse_type_annotation` is reserved for JSDoc tag-type payloads (`{Type}` text inside `@type`/`@param`/`@returns`). Calling it from the resolver / projector / registry / policy / materialiser / compat pipeline is the bug.
   952	- Raw display strings (`Analyzed*Field.type_annotation`, `ExpandedField.raw_type`, `ResolvedLocalType.expanded`, `PropMeta.rawType`) are display passthroughs only. Resolver and compat consumers MUST NOT parse them back into `TypeExpr` / `TypeDescriptor`.
   953	- Workspace classification uses `ResolverContext::workspace_is_package_backed(canonical_id)` — the single structural predicate (workspace-owned is its complement; there is no separate `workspace_is_workspace_owned` predicate). Substring checks on canonical paths (`"/node_modules/"`, `"\\node_modules\\"`) are banned. The classification API is path-agnostic and handles symlinked / pnpm-hoisted / Windows-backslash / workspace-linked-package cases.
   954	- Hand-rolled type-text parsers must not exist inside the resolver. Walk `TypeExpr` nodes — `IndexedAccess`, `Ref { name: "Pick", type_arguments }`, `Union`, `Intersection`, etc. — directly via Rust pattern matching.
   955	- The JS compat layer reads `prop.type` (`TypeDescriptor`) for every semantic decision. `prop.rawType` is display passthrough only. Operator splits use union/intersection tag matching on `TypeDescriptor`, not hand-rolled string operator parsers.
   956	
   957	If a new requirement appears to need text manipulation inside the resolver, fix the producer (lower the right OXC node, store the right typed field, extend `@verter/type-ir` with a missing variant) rather than reparsing or pattern-matching on text. Architecture-guard tests in `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/architecture_guards.rs` and equivalents in `packages/component-meta` lock down this contract.
   958	
   959	See `/component-meta` skill for the full producer-side schema (typed `*_expr` fields on `Analyzed*Field`, `ResolvedLocalType.type_expr` "always populated" invariant) and the post-cutover delete list.
   960	
   961	### Typed Value Domain + Demand-Lattice Resolution (CRITICAL)
   962	
   963	The U2 query-value-domain design (`docs/arch/u2-query-value-domain-design.md`) locks the typed value
   964	domain and the demand-lattice that decides cache satisfaction/backfill. Resolution is typed end to
   965	end; display is a projection; error and absorbing types ride existing carriers.
   966	
   967	- **One key → one value arm.** Every `SemanticQueryKey` maps to exactly one `SemanticQueryValue` arm.
   968	  No non-type value is smuggled into `GraphTypeNode`; the wire taxonomy stays a closed type taxonomy.
   969	- **Demand lattice (presets, not enum order).** The five mode names (`Identity` / `Navigate` /
   970	  `Shallow` / `Expanded` / `Skeleton`) are PRESETS over `(ProjectionDemand, EvalPolicy)`. Cache
   971	  satisfaction and backfill are decided by lattice DOMINANCE over a RECORDED materialised
   972	  `(path, point)` set — NOT by enum order, and NOT by a meet-derived nominal demand. `Skeleton` =
   973	  `TypeParamShells` + carrier-stop; it is INCOMPARABLE to the expansion presets, a regime of its own.
   974	- **Display is a projection.** Canonical display is computed at publish from the cached typed value,
   975	  never a stored or re-parsed string. `display_needs` is display-only: it is masked OUT of every
   976	  typed-value family key and never drives resolution. Two queries differing only in `display_needs`
   977	  hit the SAME typed-value slot.
   978	- **Error tolerance.** A result computed over torn / broken / mid-edit input is `ReturnOnly` and is
   979	  never warm-admitted. A fact-rooted error (a recorded missing-dep fact) IS cacheable. `admit_decision`
   980	  gates on the ROOTING FACT's presence in the `ReadSetSignature`, not on the taint class.
   981	- **Error / any / never / unknown.** `unknown` = ⊤, `never` = ⊥; `any` is off-order (relates
   982	  bidirectionally); `error` taints and rides the EXISTING `SemanticNodeData::Opaque(QueryError)`. NO
   983	  new `GraphTypeNode::ErrorType` wire arm may be introduced — the wire-purity closure forbids it.
   984	- **Planned STAGE-B guards (gap tracked here per the architecture-guard rule).** The discriminating
   985	  behavioural guards land with STAGE-B: `cache_satisfaction_is_demand_lattice_not_enum_order` (U10),
   986	  `cache_satisfaction_is_materialized_point_not_nominal_demand`,
   987	  `display_needs_is_display_only_never_drives_resolution`,
   988	  `error_tolerance_broken_input_is_returnonly_fact_rooted_error_is_cacheable`, and
   989	  `error_any_never_propagation_lattice`. The design-gate guards landed NOW are
   990	  `error_rides_opaque_no_new_error_type_wire_arm` and `u2_value_domain_design_doc_locks_invariants`
   991	  (both in `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/g_block/u2_value_domain_design_guards.rs`).
   992	
   993	## PARSELOWER Carrier Contracts (handle-migration foundation)
   994

  1009	- **Typed raise outcome (`SourceRaiseOutcome`)** — `raise_semantic_type_source_to_hot` / `raise_authored_locator_to_hot` / `raise_body_slot` return `Raised` / `Absent` / `Failed(QueryError)` instead of a bare `Option`, so absence and a swallowed typed failure are no longer one value. `Absent` is the only semantically optional non-result; `RecursionCarrier` / `ExpandableDecl` reads INTERN their `Opaque` carrier and RAISE; every other disposition travels as `Failed` with its payload intact (an `AliasCycle` keeps its participant chain). No new public output-failure variant is minted, so the closed FFI/proto contract is untouched.   1013	### Macro Hot Mirror (Stage 5A, LANDED)
  1014	
  1015	**Authored-route sidecar widening.** The historical `HotTypeRef` cell
  1016	shorthand below now means the `hot` field of one `MacroHotProduct`. Each lazy,
  1017	singleflight cell commits that handle together with graph-free per-prop
  1018	`AuthoredReferenceHeadFact` values projected from the same transient typed-IR
  1019	borrow. Requested prop classification can therefore retain an exact authored
  1020	route without a payload/body reread; the sidecar never changes semantic-node
  1021	or query identity. `macro_type_arg_hot_ref` remains the sole producer entry.
  1022	
  1023	**Authored-reference-head positions (the closed producer inventory).** Three
  1024	positions mint the graph-free `AuthoredReferenceHeadFact`, all from a transient
  1025	typed-IR borrow the producer already holds, all zero extra parse / lowering /
  1026	resolution:
  1027	
  1028	| Position | Fact field | Minter |
  1029	| --- | --- | --- |
  1030	| Value annotation | `ValueTypeAnnotationFact.reference_head` | `fact_projection::value_type_annotation_fact` |
  1031	| Macro prop payload | `MacroHotProduct.prop_reference_heads` | `fact_projection::macro_payload_reference_head_fact` |

  1033	
  1034	The return position carries an **authorship mint gate**: the head mints only
  1035	when `LoweredSignatureParts.has_authored_return` is true. `return_ty` mints its
  1036	content-free replay locator whenever the lowering produced a return carrier —
  1037	*including an inferred return* — so an ungated mint would publish authored route
  1038	evidence for a return the author never wrote (an inferred
  1039	`return x as Ref<number>` lowers to literally `Ref<number>`). Every
  1040	non-authored return position publishes `AuthoredReferenceHeadFact::Unavailable`:
  1041	inferred returns, synthesized constructors, and every OBJECT-MEMBER signature
  1042	(`member_signature_fact` passes `has_authored_return: false`). That gate is what
  1043	makes the member-position boundary structural rather than disciplinary — no
  1044	member position can mint or read a head. An authored annotation that is not a
  1045	type reference publishes `NotReference`, which the demand side treats as a
  1046	COMPLETE non-wrapper proof.
  1047	
  1048	Signature locators rebase with their overload group. `EvalEnv::add_value` →
  1049	`rebase_value_signature_ordinals` (`type_eval.rs`) re-points the leading
  1050	`ValueSignature { ordinal }` step of THREE locator families when a declaration
  1051	joins a merged overload group: the parameter slots, the return slot, and the
  1052	return head's `TypeArgLocator` argument paths. The head's locator is a
  1053	`TypeArgLocator`, not a `TypeBodySlot`, so the repointer is generalized over the
  1054	`path` position; a rebase typed to the slot alone leaves every contributor's
  1055	head addressing overload ordinal 0 — the wrong overload
  1056	(`overload_group_signature_locators_take_group_ordinals`).
  1057	
  1058	The head participates in the deep producer-local anchor walks:
  1059	`TypeArgLocator::absolutize` (`locators.rs`) plus
  1060	`AuthoredReferenceArgLocator::absolutize` /
  1061	`AuthoredReferenceHeadFact::absolutize` and
  1062	`authored_reference_head_scope_relative` (`facts.rs`), both written generically
  1063	over the head fact so every head-bearing position shares one walk. Only the
  1064	ARGUMENT anchors decide scope-relativity; the authored local spelling is route
  1065	evidence the demand resolves against the route's recorded owner, and is never
  1066	rewritten.
  1067	
  1068	The **macro hot mirror** (`crate::structural_carrier_producer::macro_arg_producer`, the single private producer module) is the SOLE production producer of a macro type-argument's structural carrier graph. `MacroHotMirror` lives on `IndexedReady`, keyed `(owner, whole_hash, macro_index)` → `MacroHotProduct` (lazy / singleflight / content-addressed `OnceLock<Option<Arc<MacroHotProduct>>>` per macro index); its `hot` field is the historical graph handle. `macro_type_arg_hot_ref(ctx, file, macro_index)` is the sole production entry. The mirror is PURE: it performs NO host route lookup and emits NO dependency facts — it only produces the UNRESOLVED structural carrier graph (the `BareRef` / `ImportType` / operator-shell carriers, resolved on demand at the consuming dispatch) via the mode-neutral `lower_type_expr_structural`, plus the graph-free authored-head sidecar described above. Script-setup `generic="T"` binders are SEEDED at build (lower to the `SemanticNodeData::TypeParam` binder, not `BareRef(T)`); macro-own-body provenance (`declared_in_macro_type_arg`) is baked at production time. Direct dispatch lowering of an authored SFC macro shell must likewise use `lower_type_expr_in_owner_scope_with_mode` with the macro's recorded owner. The owner-agnostic convenience entry denotes the ordinary/module owner; it cannot infer that a synthetic test expression came from `<script setup>`, and callers must not compensate with file-wide or get-any owner matching.
  1069	
  1070	**Single-producer guarantee — TWO confinement regimes + bounded same-module policing.** The producer-capable code is COLLAPSED into ONE private module, `crate::structural_carrier_producer::macro_arg_producer`, declared as a private `mod macro_arg_producer;` that re-exports EXACTLY `pub(crate) use macro_arg_producer::{macro_type_arg_hot_ref, MacroHotMirror};`. The THREE producer-capable builders — `lower_type_expr_structural`, the macro hot-mirror builder `build_macro_hot_ref`, and the `<script setup generic="…">` binder-seed builder `build_script_setup_seed_frames` — are EACH a BARE module-private fn (no visibility modifier) inside that one file. (1) The FOREIGN case is COMPILER-CONFINED: no module outside `macro_arg_producer` can NAME any of the three builders — a foreign reference is a compile error (E0603 / E0433), so a second producer in a foreign file is unrepresentable by construction. (2) The SAME-MODULE case is NOT compiler-confined — Rust privacy is module-scoped, so a SECOND producer written INSIDE `macro_arg_producer.rs` CAN name the module-private builders, and the collapse to one file does not make that a compile error. That same-module residual is POLICED by the strengthened single-producer architecture guards, which together cover the 8-category same-module exposure surface: `structural_carrier_producer_lowerer_is_module_private` pins ALL THREE builders bare-private + single-defined + not re-exported; `macro_hot_mirror_exposes_single_crate_visible_producer_entry` is the producer-EXPOSURE collector — `macro_type_arg_hot_ref` is the ONLY crate-visible producer entry, covering module-level FREE fns AND INHERENT-impl associated fns under a cfg-SATISFIABILITY test-gate classifier (an item is test-only ONLY when its `#[cfg]` ENTAILS test — `#[cfg(any(test, debug_assertions))]` / `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "x"))]` are PRODUCTION-satisfiable and COUNTED, closing the prior over-exclusion), PLUS crate-visible VALUE exposure (`const`/`static`/associated-const fn-pointers of a builder), PLUS TRAIT exposure (only the hand-written `Debug`/`Clone` for `MacroHotMirror`; any other trait impl / trait def/alias reds), PLUS the EXACT `mod.rs` re-export-shape pin (private module decl + exactly the two-leaf `pub(crate) use`, no alias/glob/extra leaf/widened decl); `macro_arg_producer_has_no_production_expansion_surface` bans ALL production bang-macro invocations (a denylist is incomplete because a macro defined elsewhere and invoked here is invisible to `syn`; the one `matches!` and the one `vec!` are de-sugared to keep the file bang-macro-free) plus `macro_rules!` / proc-macro attributes / `#[macro_use]` / out-of-line-or-`#[path]` child mods (only `#[cfg(test)] #[path] mod *_tests;` wiring is allowed) plus the SCOPED derive rules — derive paths must be single-segment built-ins (a qualified `evil::Debug` reds) and NO production import / glob / `#[macro_use]` may shadow a built-in-derive name into scope (the module KEEPS its `#[derive(Debug, Clone, …)]`); `session_graph_lowerer_makes_no_query` + `macro_hot_mirror_producer_is_pure_no_route_resolution` ban the QUERY/DISPATCH route (`.dispatch(`, `lower_type_expr_in_scope_with_`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, `SemanticQueryKey`, the route-resolving `ensure_indexed_ready(` — DISTINCT from the allowed route-free `ensure_indexed_ready_serve`, prepared-decl/route helpers) — a producer that route-resolves would be a SECOND query-time resolution engine; and `no_production_macro_arg_eager_lowering_outside_mirror` is the file-scope ordering tripwire. The IRREDUCIBLE residual NOT covered by either regime is trust in the one sanctioned producer implementation plus compiler bugs / build-time substitution / out-of-tree proc-macros — by design. The FOUR production graph-lowering uses of a macro `parsed_type_argument` all read the ONE mirror handle and re-enter the shared dispatch from it for their TERMINAL demand (no site lowers the macro arg a second time): the `resolve_macro_payload` projector + silent-miss probe (`meta_resolve/projectors/mod.rs`), the slot-binding extractor (`meta_resolve/slot_binding_graph.rs`), the `vue_exec` `defineSlots<mapped>` / graph-native indexed-access decompose (`typeinfo/framework_surface/vue_exec/mod.rs`), and `eval_env` `expand_macro_types` + `defineModel` (`host_manage/eval_env.rs`).

  1072	**Demand-site carrier resolution + dep recording (codex-ruled "A/C, not B").** The mirror is query-free, so it DEFERS the resolution eager lowering did eagerly (TypeOf value-root execution, Pick/utility source resolution, cross-file resolution-witness recording). Per the architecture ruling, resolution + dep recording happen at the resolving DEMAND, never as a side-band dep preflight on the mirror accessor (a second traversal policy is forbidden). The demand sites: `resolve_carrier_subject_node` (`carrier.rs`) resolves a `TypeOf` carrier subject (the empty-path `typeof config` macro payload — the walker's per-segment `TypeOf` arm never fires for an empty path) via `typeof_key_for` → `build_typeof` (resolve → project the carrier path in `Navigate` → apply `type_args`); a NON-empty `ProjectPath` path leaves the TypeOf base for the walker's mid-walk arm. The deferred-shell evaluator (`evaluate.rs`) resolves a `BareRef`/`ImportType` source carrier (Pick/Omit source, mapped source) one hop under `StructuralTransit(Navigate)`. `resolve_member_value_for_classification` (the exactness path) resolves a bare/import carrier so `type MyStr = string` classifies `ExactConcrete`. **Resolution-witness recording:** `build_typeof`'s import miss (a `typeof <unresolved import>`) observes the owner's path-precise resolution witness into the active tracer and marks `result_is_partial` + `cache_suppress` + the request materialization-suppress sticky. A genuine `MissingDependency` is `ReturnOnly`; the field materializer refuses `ShapeCacheDb` admission of a `TypeOf`-rooted semantic miss so the next request after the dependency appears recomputes cold and recovers.

  1074	**Macro-surface partiality carries typed completeness; warm dispatch hits are NOT budget-debited (codex decider).** A macro surface that resolves through the shared dispatch carries a typed `ResultCompleteness` (`semantic_query.rs`). `vue_macro_dtos_with_ctx` (`vue_exec/mod.rs`) returns `MacroDtosRead { dtos, completeness }`, wraps its cold compute in a `ColdComputeCompletenessScope`, and admits the bundle into `vue_surface_store` ONLY when `completeness == Complete` AND `finalise == Ok` — a GENUINE partial DTO bundle is returned to the caller but never enters the surface store (no laundered warm replay). All DTO consumers (`define_shapes`, `slot_binding_graph::typeinfo_macro_dtos`, `resolver_core::component_meta`) fold the surface's partiality into the request-result completeness via `MacroDtosRead::observe_partial()`; the framework-surface executor surfaces `ResolvedOutcome::Partial`. `ResolvedComponentMetaState.completeness` is the authoritative per-result partial signal; `synthesis_should_suppress` is its compatibility projection (`= completeness.is_partial()`), preserved across the `ComponentMetaResultDb` `ResolutionTemplate` round-trip. The decider EXPLICITLY forbids charging warm cache hits to re-trip the projection budget (the budget is a runaway FUSE, not a semantic-complexity quota; charging warm hits risks false partials for complete-warmed work). **Per-result no-poison (LANDED):** the discriminating fixture `batch_partial_returned_never_admitted_while_complete_sibling_warms` (32 non-overlapping interfaces = 96 distinct props, `projection_op_budget = 6`, an unbounded oracle host) pins the invariant by typed completeness + admission-refusal, NOT a prop-count threshold: a result OBSERVED `Partial` (batch 1's budget-tripped cold compute) is REFUSED at the fixed-view cache boundary and never warmed (the primary discriminator); a genuine `Complete` recompute after warm resolver memos heal MAY admit (valid healing, not laundering — the partial result itself is never promoted). The discrimination is pinned by a `store_stable`-gate flip (`component_meta_request.rs:372`) that reddens the batch-1 `!result_admitted` witness. (The earlier 13-prop `<18` fixture rested on a non-deterministic budget re-trip the content-addressed mirror legitimately removed; it was corrected, not weakened — no rule exception, no carve-out. See `docs/arch/parselower-design.md` Stage 5A residual.)

  1083	
  1084	## Flow-Return Substrate (U6)
  1085	
  1086	The whole-function flow-return capability (`U6.FLOW_RETURN_SUBSTRATE`) is a demand-sliced substrate over four artifacts plus one dispatch arm:
  1087	
  1088	- **`FunctionBodySkeleton`** (`crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/flow/mod.rs`) — an arena-free (`Send + Sync + 'static`, `NoTypeExpr`) shallow statement/control skeleton with a return-site index, a lexical binding index, assignment/kill summaries, and per-site read/write/call + object-literal property footprints. Built once per function content version from the retained parse snapshot; NO type lowering at build time. **Which sub-expressions become their own tracked SITE is not this builder's own judgement**: `SkeletonBuilder::open_site` dispatches on `analysis::flow::value_descent`, the ONE wildcard-free classifier of an expression's value-structural children, and the content half's `Lowerer::lower_expr` dispatches on the SAME verdict. That is the structural fix for a planner/content split: a conditional expression got a structural arm in the CONTENT half while the planner still had no reason to descend into a branch, so every object literal in a branch lowered with each member value on the typed `SliceExpr::Elided` carrier and the whole return failed closed (`k ? { a: 1 } : 2` — `Error(Miss)` cands=0 — while `k ? {} : 2`, with no member value to elide, stayed green: the signature of an under-selected PLAN, not a broken arm). Neither half carries an UNDISPOSITIONED wildcard over `Expression` any more. `lower_expr` does end in `other => match value_descent(other)` — the wildcard is a DELEGATION, not a disposition: the wildcard-free match lives in the classifier, so a new variant does not compile until it is dispositioned THERE, and both halves inherit that disposition in the same change. `ValueDescent::TypeCarrier` is the ONE named asymmetry (the planner descends so a projection into the literal still reaches its members) — under-selection is the bug, and over-selection is not free: the content half's leaf answer for a carrier over a literal with a CALL-sourced spread embeds the spread's unreduced `ReturnType<callee>` carrier, which the leaf's fabricated-value gate refuses, so ONE carrier failed the whole RETURN closed for a value the checker types. So the content half no longer swallows a carrier over an OBJECT LITERAL: the literal keeps its structural lowering and the carrier contributes a MEMBER POLICY instead — see "Object-literal entry lowering" below. Every other carrier still leaf-lowers whole, because its type genuinely is the carrier's rather than its operand's.
  1089	
  1090	**Object-literal entry lowering never abandons the literal for ONE entry.** The fallback to the whole-literal leaf answer is not local: it folds every sibling, spreads included, into one shallow-pass answer, and a leaf answer over a CALL-sourced spread embeds the callee's unreduced `ReturnType<…>` carrier, which the fabricated-value gate refuses. One unmodellable ENTRY therefore failed the whole RETURN closed. Two entry families no longer reach it:
  1091	
  1092	- **A key whose property name is not its authored text** (`{ ...base(), [k]: 1 }`, `{ ...base(), 1: 2 }`) lowers as its OWN value position — `SliceObjectKey::Computed { value, authored }`. The evaluator names the property from the key's evaluated LITERAL (numeric keys through the SHARED canonical spelling, so `{ 1: x }` is the number `1`, never the string `"1"`); a key whose value is OPEN (`[key]` with `key: string`) leaves the surface's key SET unknown, which an object surface cannot express, so the literal fails CLOSED exactly as an unevaluable spread source does — publishing the modelled siblings alone would declare a member set missing a key the authored value has. The `authored` half is the second channel for the one nameable key the value channel cannot carry: a `unique symbol` key, whose value flattens to the bare `symbol` primitive.
  1093	- **A type carrier over an object literal** contributes an `ObjectMemberPolicy` (`Widen` / `Preserve` / `ConstAssert`) rather than swallowing the literal. The three states mirror the shared shallow pass's own object-literal widening contexts exactly, because a carrier that lowers structurally and one that reaches the leaf lowering must not disagree about the same literal. `as const` pins every member literal AND marks the literal's own members `readonly`; `satisfies` preserves uniformly (this substrate performs no contextual typing, so the target-driven half of tsc's rule is the deferred contextual-widening contract — `flow_return_catalog::flow_return_ob05_satisfies_preserves_value_shape` pins the preserving side).
  1094	
  1095	Two recorded divergences ride this, both asserted rather than silent: a SPREAD-contributed member does not take an enclosing `as const`'s `readonly` (the spread program merges the source's own modifiers — the existing spread-path `readonly` gap, reached by one more shape), and a `unique symbol` key keeps the member under a COMPUTED key rather than its nominal identity (`flow_return_ob12_keeps_unique_symbol_computed_key_shape`). Acceptance: `typeinfo_tests::value_inference::object_return_entry_forms_lower_structurally_over_a_call_spread` is the PRIMARY semantic pin against tsgo `7.0.0-dev.20260526.1`; `meta_tests::an_entry_form_over_a_call_spread_reaches_the_runtime_lane_intact` and `cases::g_block::framework_surface_executor::an_entry_form_over_a_call_spread_reaches_the_framework_surface_intact` are secondary evidence that the answer survives to a consumer.
  1096	
  1097	**Object-literal ENTRY classification is a second shared classifier on the same module** (`analysis::flow::value_descent`): `object_entry_descent(&ObjectPropertyKind) -> ObjectEntryDescent` splits an entry into `Property { key: ObjectEntryKey, value, kind: ObjectEntryKind, property }` or `Spread { source }`, with `object_entry_key` / `static_property_key_text` as the single authority for how a key NAMES its property (`Static` for an identifier or string literal, `Computed` for a computed or NUMERIC-literal key — `{ 1: x }`'s authored text is not its property name — `Unmodeled` for a private name). Accessor kinds are decided BEFORE the `method` shorthand flag, so a getter is never called a method. The classifier's guarantee is scoped: it is the single authority for the KEY and for the entry SHAPE, consumed by the skeleton's `open_object_site` and the content half's `lower_object_literal`. It is NOT the only site that decides an entry's KIND — `type_eval_build::extract_object_literal` (the shallow-pass leaf lowering the content half falls back to) and `function_program`'s property-footprint indexing each carry their own `PropertyKind` match. No behavioural divergence is measured (the precedences agree), and unifying them is not this substrate's boundary; the scoped claim is recorded here so the "single authority" phrasing is not read wider than it holds. The classifier answers a SECOND question on the same pass: `ValueDescent::UnmodeledCall` names a form whose OWN value is a call's return with no structural arm (`new f()`, `` tag`…` ``, `f?.()`, `await f()`, `(k, f())`, and a call under a type carrier), decided by the single predicate `analysis::flow::value_is_unmodeled_call` — the CONTENT half fails closed, the PLANNER half takes the `Leaf` disposition (a call's arguments never provide its value). That verdict moved here because it is a property of the FORM: the downstream carrier gate reads the leaf ANSWER, and for all of those forms the shallow pass answers a bare `any` with no carrier in it, so nothing fired and a fabricated `any` published warm and clean under a promise that a call with no structural arm fails closed. The skeleton records the branch arms as `SkeletonExprShape::BranchJoin`, and the graph turns them into `ValueDef` edges, so the demanded path threads through both arms UNCHANGED.   1149	- **The demand-sliced substrate is the ONLY flow evaluator.** A `FlowReturn` cold path plans the demand slice as graph reachability (`FunctionBodySkeleton` → `FunctionFlowGraph` → `ReturnPathPeeker`), hashes it (`FlowSliceHashNode`), lowers exactly the plan into the content-free `FlowSliceIR` (`FlowSliceLoweredBodyNode`), and evaluates through the slice-gated owned content (`crates/verter_session/src/flow_slice_content.rs` — `SliceContent`, produced per demand through the `DeclBodyMemo` lease-only retained-snapshot run). Content OUTSIDE the slice never lowers: an unread binding initializer is omitted (the gate is the `FlowSlot` binding-identifier SPAN, declaration-precise — a shadowed same-named sibling declarator the plan kept out never lowers), a sibling member value rides the typed `SliceExpr::Elided` carrier (fail-closed if ever observed), and `if`-test / expression-statement positions carry no content. Selected leaf expressions lower through the ONE shared shallow-pass per-expression entry `infer_declaration_expression_type` (literal-preserving for arrow bodies / `const` initializers, widening otherwise). There is no whole-body evaluator and no separate return scanner; a leaf-lowering budget edge can only be charged by SELECTED content (guarded by `flow_return_unread_binding_content_never_lowers` / `flow_return_member_demand_never_lowers_elided_sibling_content`).

The non-strict branch (plain `T`, e.g. `number`) is NOT modeled by the flow-return substrate and remains U6.VALUE_INFERENCE debt — do not "fix" the strict branch to the non-strict answer.

Until that lands, a lowered slice carrying a whole-slot write effect targeting a parameter or a value-selected slot fails CLOSED as the `UnappliedWriteEffect` DEGRADED SUCCESS (`ReturnOnly`, never warm) — evaluating past the write could publish a wrong type as complete (assignment narrowing; object members evaluate left-to-right). (a) **Conditional definitions fail closed.** A conditional-arm nesting counter rises on `if` ARMS only — a plain block executes unconditionally and never increments it — and a `var` bound under non-zero nesting enters `var_conditional_locals`; OBSERVING such a binding records the `ConditionalVarDefinition` degradation (`ReturnOnly`, never warm), mirroring `var_degraded_locals` exactly, so an unobserved conditional `var` degrades nothing and an unconditional rebind clears the flag. A serve or index miss has nothing to hand over and returns `CalleeClauseLookup::Unavailable` (or `None`), which routes to the `UnrepresentableCallee` degradation. The two routes are now SYMMETRIC on a miss: `instantiate_callee_clause_at_unknown` used to return the callee's body-derived return UNTOUCHED — its own binders published warm — where the call-site route degraded on the identical miss. Collapsing that into "the callee is not generic" is how a lookup FAILURE hands the callee's return back verbatim, binders and all, with no degradation and full warm admission. The SCC fixed point is confined the same way: a hold carries its callee's clause (`HeldCallee`), and `HeldCallee::discharged` is the only accessor turning a hold target's admitted result into a join arm, so the equation cannot re-run the transfer around the gate. Exactly one exemption exists and is named: `HeldCallee::own_frame`, the direct SELF-call, whose callee IS the calling frame — its binders are the frame's own and must survive (`f<T>(x: T): T` stays `T`, not `T | unknown`).

     2	name: rust-performance
     3	description: "Rust performance optimization patterns: batch operations, allocation hierarchy, object pooling, CodeTransform API for verter_compiler"
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Rust Performance Guide
     7	
     8	Principles for writing performant Rust in `verter_compiler`.
     9	
    10	## 1. Batch Over Incremental
    11	
    12	`CodeTransform` operations like `overwrite()` and `prepend_left()` each walk the chunk list in O(n). Calling them in a loop is O(n\*N). Collect operations into `Vec`s and apply with batch APIs:
    13	
    14	- `batch_overwrite(ops: &[(u32, u32, &str)])` — sorted overwrites in one chunk-list pass
    15	- `batch_prepend_left_static(ops: &[(u32, &str)])` — sorted inserts in one pass
    16	
    17	```rust
    18	// BAD: O(n) per call × N calls
    19	for (start, end, content) in replacements {
    20	    code_transform.overwrite(start, end, content);
    21	}
    22	
    23	// GOOD: O(n+m) single pass
    24	replacements.sort_by_key(|(start, _, _)| *start);
    25	code_transform.batch_overwrite(&replacements);
    26	```
    27	
    28	If calling a mutating method in a loop, ask whether operations can be collected and applied in one traversal.
    29	
    30	## 2. Allocation Hierarchy
    31	
    32	Prefer allocations in this order (fastest to slowest):
    33	
    34	1. **`&'static str`** — zero-cost, compile-time constants
    35	2. **`&'alloc str`** via `code_transform.alloc_str(buf)` — OXC bump allocator, freed in bulk
    36	3. **`&str`** from `ctx.input[start..end]` — zero-cost slice of source
    37	4. **Reusable `&mut String` buffer** — amortized cost via capacity reuse
    38	5. **`String`** — heap-allocated, avoid in hot paths
    39	
    40	| Need | Use |
    41	| ---- | --- |
    42	| Known constant value | `&'static str` |
    43	| Generated text that outlives current function | `code_transform.alloc_str(buf)` → `&'alloc str` |
    44	| Substring of source input | `&ctx.input[start..end]` |
    45	| Temporary text build-up | Shared `&mut String` buffer (see below) |
    46	| Truly owned, long-lived, mutable text | `String` |
    47	
    48	## 3. Reusable Buffer Pattern
    49	
    50	Codegen generators (e.g., `VdomTemplateGenerator`) keep a `buf: String` field. Use `std::mem::take` to temporarily take ownership — avoids borrow conflicts with other `self` fields:
    51	
    52	```rust
    53	// Take buffer — avoids per-element heap allocation:
    54	let mut buf = std::mem::take(&mut self.buf);
    55	process_element(&mut buf, ...);
    56	self.buf = buf; // return — retains capacity for next element
    57	
    58	// In called functions, accept buf: &mut String.
    59	// Use `buf` directly, not `&mut buf` (it's already &mut String).
    60	```
    61	
    62	After building text in `buf`, persist via bump allocator:
    63	
    64	```rust
    65	buf.clear();
    66	buf.push_str("_createVNode(");
    67	buf.push_str(tag);
    68	buf.push(')');
    69	let s: &'alloc str = code_transform.alloc_str(&buf);
    70	pending_overwrites.push((start, end, s));
    71	```
    72	
    73	### Save/Truncate for Nested Buffer Use
    74	
    75	To build a temporary string inside a function already using `buf`, use save/truncate instead of allocating a second buffer:
    76	
    77	```rust
    78	let saved = buf.len();
    79	buf.push_str("{ ");
    80	for (i, prop) in props.iter().enumerate() {
    81	    if i > 0 { buf.push_str(", "); }
    82	    buf.push_str(prop);
    83	}
    84	buf.push_str(" }");
    85	let result = code_transform.alloc_str(&buf[saved..]);
    86	buf.truncate(saved); // restore buf to previous state
    87	```
    88	
    89	Avoids per-element heap allocation when building intermediate strings like hoisted props.
    90	
    91	## 4. Object Pooling
    92	
    93	`StateStack` (per-element state during tree walk) contains multiple `Vec` fields. Pool instead of allocating/dropping per element:
    94	
    95	```rust
    96	// Take from pool — Vecs retain capacity from previous use:
    97	fn take_state(&mut self, id: u32) -> StateStack {
    98	    if let Some(mut s) = self.state_pool.pop() {
    99	        s.reset(id);  // .clear() on all Vecs — retains capacity
   100	        s
   101	    } else {
   102	        StateStack { id, ..Default::default() }
   103	    }
   104	}
   105	
   106	// Return to pool after element close:
   107	fn return_state(&mut self, state: StateStack) {
   108	    self.state_pool.push(state);
   109	}
   110	```
   111	
   112	Apply to any struct with inner collections repeatedly created/dropped in a loop. `Vec::clear()` retains allocated capacity.
   113	
   114	## 5. Borrow Source Instead of Cloning
   115	
   116	`ctx.input` holds the full source text. Borrow slices directly instead of cloning:
   117	
   118	```rust
   119	// BAD: heap allocation just to read
   120	let name: String = ctx.input[start..end].to_string();
   121	buf.push_str(&name);
   122	
   123	// GOOD: zero-cost borrow
   124	let name: &str = &ctx.input[start as usize..end as usize];
   125	buf.push_str(name);
   126	```
   127	
   128	For struct fields, prefer `&'alloc str` (bump-allocated) when the struct's lifetime allows. If adding a lifetime would cascade through too many types, `String` is acceptable.
   129	
   130	## 6. Static Fast Paths
   131	
   132	For functions frequently returning one of a small set of constants, return `&'static str` directly. `&'static str` coerces to `&'alloc str`, so static constants can be used anywhere bump-allocated strings are expected.
   133	
   134	```rust
   135	// Common close strings — no bump allocation needed
   136	let close_str: &'alloc str = if patch_flag.0 == 0 && !is_block_root {
   137	    if needs_array { "])" } else { ")" }  // &'static str coerces to &'alloc str
   138	} else {
   139	    // Rare case: build dynamically
   140	    buf.clear();
   141	    write_patch_flag_suffix(buf, patch_flag, &dynamic_props);
   142	    code_transform.alloc_str(buf)
   143	};
   144	```
   145	
   146	## 7. Pre-size Collections
   147	
   148	Use `with_capacity` when expected size is known or estimable:
   149	
   150	```rust
   151	pending_overwrites: Vec::with_capacity(512),
   152	pending_prepend_lefts: Vec::with_capacity(256),
   153	buf: String::with_capacity(128),
   154	```
   155	
   156	Over-estimating slightly is cheaper than re-allocating.
   157	
   158	## 8. Reduce Work, Not Just Speed
   159	
   160	Once allocation and batching are optimized, further gains come from doing less work:
   161	
   162	- **Skip expensive operations for trivial cases** — e.g., don't sort prop indices when all props have the same priority, don't run OXC parser for a bare identifier binding
   163	- **Early-return fast paths** — e.g., skip Vec allocation + sort + clone when all element props are static (no directives)
   164	- **Merge redundant operations** — e.g., combine two adjacent overwrites (tag name + props) into a single overwrite when both are known at the same time
   165	- **Cache/deduplicate repeated computations** — e.g., `resolved_components_set` for component dedup
   166	- **Short-circuit early** when results are known
   167	
   168	## 9. Bulk-Copy String Processing
   169	
   170	When processing strings character-by-character (e.g., escaping), prefer a bulk-copy pattern that tracks unmodified regions and copies them in one `push_str` call:
   171	
   172	```rust
   173	fn escape_js_string_into(buf: &mut String, s: &str) {
   174	    let mut last_copy_end = 0;
   175	    for (i, ch) in s.char_indices() {
   176	        let replacement = match ch {
   177	            '"' => "\\\"",
   178	            '\\' => "\\\\",
   179	            '\n' => "\\n",
   180	            _ => continue,
   181	        };
   182	        buf.push_str(&s[last_copy_end..i]); // bulk copy unmodified region
   183	        buf.push_str(replacement);
   184	        last_copy_end = i + ch.len_utf8();
   185	    }
   186	    buf.push_str(&s[last_copy_end..]); // copy remaining
   187	}
   188	```
   189	
   190	## 10. Benchmarking Methodology
   191	
   192	When comparing against another compiler (e.g., Vue's `@vue/compiler-sfc`):
   193	
   194	- **Ensure feature parity** — if one compiler generates source maps and the other doesn't, you're not comparing the same work
   195	- **Source maps are expensive** — VLQ encoding + JSON serialization + base64 can consume 30-40% of compile time
   196	- **NAPI overhead is fixed** — allocator creation + JS↔Rust marshalling adds ~7μs per call
   197	- **Profile in release mode** — debug builds are 10-50x slower
   198	
   199	### Agent Profiling via MCP (hotpath)
   200	
   201	```bash
   202	pnpm run profile:hotpath:mcp    # Start with MCP endpoint at http://localhost:6771/mcp
   203	pnpm run profile:hotpath        # Timing hotspots (no MCP)
   204	pnpm run profile:hotpath:alloc  # Timing + allocation hotspots
   205	```
   206	
   207	Agent MCP config template: `mcp/hotpath.mcp.json`
   208	
   209	## 11. CodeTransform Optimization History
   210	
   211	### Successful Optimizations (Committed)
   212	
   213	**A. Fast-path `overwrite()` for single Original chunk** — When the overwritten range falls within a single Original chunk, bypass the general `SmallVec<[Chunk; 4]>` + `Vec::splice` path. Use direct `Vec::insert` (1-2 calls) for the 4 sub-cases.
   214	
   215	**B. Eliminate `build_string` first pass via `output_delta` tracking** — Added `output_delta: i64` field tracking running difference between inserted and removed content. `build_string()` uses it for `String::with_capacity`, eliminating the first chunk-iteration pass. ~19% improvement on `build_string/2000`.
   216	
   217	**C. Merge `move_wrapped` split + identification into single pass** — Replaced 3 separate linear scans with a single forward `while` loop.
   218	
   219	**E-H. Scratch Vec pre-allocation, push_u32 direct digit computation, format_patch_flag static strings, provided_locals Option optimization** — Combined: compile aggregate -9.4%.
   220	
   221	**K-N. format_scope_close → &'static str, children.rs text run static constants, condition_scope_close, build_child_records prefix optimization** — Combined: no_sourcemap -5.0%, with_sourcemap -8% to -17%.
   222	
   223	### Failed/Reverted Optimizations
   224	
   225	**D. PositionSweep for monotonic positions** — Changing `emit_mapped_content`'s function signature caused +8.7% regression on unmodified files. Binary search with ~10 comparisons is already in the CPU branch predictor's sweet spot.
   226	
   227	**I. BindingContext clone elimination** — Inconclusive due to 20-33% system noise. BindingContext clone cost is small (one FxHashSet per expression).
   228	
   229	**O. Vec<ChildRecord> reuse via std::mem::take** — No measurable improvement. Small Vec allocations (1-10 items) are already efficient.
   230	
   231	### Where NOT to Look for Further Gains
   232	
   233	| Area | Why it won't help |
   234	| ---- | ----------------- |
   235	| `offset_to_line_col` binary search | Already fast for typical file sizes |
   236	| `emit_mapped_content` signature | Changing parameters causes LLVM optimization regressions |
   237	| `memchr_iter` in source map | Already optimal — memchr uses SIMD |
   238	| `Vec<ChildRecord>` reuse | Small Vec allocations (1-10 items) are already fast |
   239	| `resolve_simple_expr` per-expression String | ~10-20 calls per component, ~20 bytes each — below noise floor |
   240	| Component resolution String allocation | Per-component, unavoidable (tag names are dynamic) |
   241	
   242	## Anti-Patterns
   243	
   244	| Pattern | Problem | Fix |
   245	| ------- | ------- | --- |
   246	| `overwrite()`/`prepend_left()` in a loop | O(n) per call | Collect into Vec + batch API |
   247	| `buf.clone()` for storage | Heap alloc per clone | `code_transform.alloc_str(buf)` |
   248	| `.to_string()` on `ctx.input` slices | Unnecessary heap copy | `&ctx.input[start..end]` |
   249	| Fresh Vec-heavy structs per iteration | Alloc/dealloc churn | Pool + `reset()` with `.clear()` |
   250	| `Instant::now()` unconditionally | Panics in WASM | `#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]` guard |
   251	| SmallVec with large types (>64B) in Box'd structs | Inflates allocation size, 40-50% regression | Keep `Vec` |
   252	| `Vec<String>` for bump-allocatable content | Per-element heap alloc | `Vec<&'alloc str>` + save/truncate |
   253	| Explicit `is_sorted` check before sort | Rust's TimSort already detects sorted runs | Just call `.sort_by_key()` |
   254	| Changing hot function signatures | Causes LLVM optimization regressions | Keep hot function signatures stable |
   255	| Linear sweep replacing binary search on <1K elements | Binary search already in CPU branch predictor sweet spot | Only consider at >10K elements |
   256	| Reusing small Vecs (1-10 items) | Allocator handles small allocations efficiently | Only pool/reuse Vecs with >50 items |

    14	> Does resuming the existing `PriorityFrontierState`'s pre-block completed prefix across request-local `NeedInputs` waves, owned and basis-cleared by the existing retained `ResolveFrame`, remain within ratified C1 request-local allocation/copy optimization, or does it introduce a new state-machine/semantic/cache contract? If `FIX_PATH`, specify the minimal permitted private shape and mutation/acceptance controls; if `NO_PATH`, name the exact violated invariant/authority.
    15	
    16	## Verdict
    17	
    18	Resuming a completed priority-frontier prefix across `NeedInputs` waves is not authorized as a C1-local allocation/copy optimization, even if:
    19	
    20	- retention is confined to one `ResolveFrame`;
    21	- state is cleared on basis change;
    22	- only candidates completed before the first block are retained;
    23	- every candidate at and after the first block is reevaluated;
    24	- no speculative post-block hit, miss, terminal, or blocked state is retained.
    25	
    26	It creates a request-local semantic continuation protocol across distinct immutable observation snapshots.
    27	
    28	## Decisive invariants
    29	
    30	1. The normative input-loading algorithm requires each retry to “run the whole operation against snapshot `S`” and, after extending the snapshot, “restart from step 1” (`contracts/input-loading.md`, §4 steps 1 and 10). Starting at the previous first-block candidate is not a whole-operation restart.
    31	
    32	2. `AttemptOutput` is explicitly one fresh accumulator per attempt. A `NeedInputs` or `Terminal` result discards that attempt's accumulator entirely; only `Complete` transfers output to the driver (`attempt_output.rs` module contract and `AttemptOutput::new`).
    33	
    34	3. Priority-frontier rules 3 and 9 are exact:
    35	
    36	   - on the first block, retain only its `LoadSet`;
    37	   - every `NeedInputs` or `Terminal` path discards all branch/frontier output.
    38	
    39	   A completed pre-block prefix necessarily contains ordered consumed-observation output. Keeping it for a later wave retains more than the `LoadSet` and later republishes output originating in a discarded attempt.
    40	
    41	4. `PriorityFrontierState` being described as “resumable” does not authorize this lifetime extension. Its documented purpose is suspending a frontier while evaluating a child frontier within one graph traversal and one attempt. It currently carries an attempt-local `AttemptOutput` and basis-local blocked set; it is not a cross-snapshot continuation token.
    42	
    43	5. The prior memo ruling permits request/`ResolveFrame`-local pure derivation reuse. A completed candidate miss is not pure request geometry: it depends on observation values and carries semantic witness output.
    44	
    45	## Why pre-block-only retention is still insufficient
    46	
    47	Excluding every speculative post-block result is necessary to preserve:
    48	
    49	- full same-basis `LoadSet` union;
    50	- bounded speculative sibling evaluation;
    51	- lower-priority-hit precedence;
    52	- terminal-after-block precedence;
    53	- reconsideration after loading.
    54	
    55	It does not solve the attempt-boundary violation.
    56	
    57	There are only two ways to skip the completed prefix:
    58	
    59	- retain its `AttemptOutput` and merge it into a later `Complete`, violating the discard contract; or
    60	- retain only a prefix cursor and reconstruct its witness later without reevaluating it, introducing a new observation-result replay/proof mechanism.
    61

   142	`new` canonicalizes upsert and tombstone keys, while `get` currently
   143	canonicalizes every lookup key. In this A6 harness no session overlay upsert or
   144	tombstone exists. Coverage records:
   145	
   146	- zero executions of both insertion-body normalizer lines at
   147	  `resolution_currency.rs:273,279` (the two iterators are empty);
   148	- 38,304 executions of the `get` normalization across the harness's four
   149	  identical passes, i.e. exactly 9,576 per pass.
   150	
   151	The empty map makes `get`'s result `None` independently of the key. Therefore
   152	the normalizer call neither establishes a fact nor influences which fact is
   153	loaded. It is not a witness-preserving requirement of the staged driver.
   154	
   155	## Exact base composition and the 244 algebra
   156	
   157	### Base call-site composition
   158	
   159	| exact calls | base source family | base call sites |
   160	|---:|---|---|
   161	| 1,368 | empty request-local overlay lookup | `resolution_currency.rs:321-325`, `ResolutionOverlaySnapshot::get` |
   162	| 6,516 | legacy live resolver path, 9 x 724 | `resolver.rs:513,1229,1265,1290,1301,1369,1405,1446,2055` |
   163	| 2,896 | live transaction observation, 4 x 724 | `resolution_currency.rs:2741,2778,2781,2789` |
   164	| 533 | Engine/workspace ingress | `engine.rs:725,1441,1468,1552,1553,1577,2398` |
   165	| **11,313** | | |
   166	
   167	The base legacy resolver rows include repeated normalization within one live
   168	resolution. The approved candidate frame/memo corrections lawfully collapse
   169	those nine calls to two first uses, reducing 6,516 to 1,448 (`-5,068`). The
   170	approved canonical transaction replay eliminates the four live observation
   171	normalizations (`-2,896`). These are exactly the two approved reduction families
   172	relevant to this corpus.
   173	
   174	The Stage-2 driver makes more reads through the immutable overlay wrapper while
   175	loading and replaying missing observations. That raises the same empty-overlay
   176	`get` call site from 1,368 to 9,576 (`+8,208`). Net:
   177	
   178	```text
   179	8,208 - 5,068 - 2,896 = 244
   180	```
   181	
   182	This explains why the candidate can have all approved provenance fixes and yet
   183	remain 244 above the base total: the large staged-overlay increase is almost,
   184	but not quite, offset by the request-local frame and replay reductions.
   185	
   186	It does **not** prove the 9,576 normalizations are required. The overlay lookups
   187	are required; canonicalizing their keys when the overlay has no entries is not.
   188	
   189	## Minimal lawful fix
   190	
   191	The permitted production change is limited to the existing private lookup in
   192	`crates/verter_workspace/src/resolution_currency.rs`:
   193	
   194	```rust
   195	fn get(&self, canonical_id: &str) -> Option<Option<Arc<str>>> {
   196	    if self.entries.is_empty() {
   197	        return None;
   198	    }
   199	    self.entries
   200	        .get(&normalize_canonical_id(canonical_id))
   201	        .cloned()
   202	}
   203	```
   204	
   205	The actual implementation should retain the fully-qualified normalizer spelling
   206	used by the file. No other code change is authorized by this report.
   207	
   208	Why this is inside the approved boundary:
   209	
   210	- the object is explicitly immutable and request-local;
   211	- the branch is in its current owner and adds no field, map, cache, memo,
   212	  retention, or cross-request state;
   213	- `get` is private, so no public API changes;
   214	- the empty case already returns `None` for every possible normalized key;
   215	- nonempty overlays still take the existing normalization path byte-for-byte;
   216	- the driver still performs the same lookup, load, retry, and replay sequence.
   217	
   218	This is smaller than introducing a canonical lookup API or changing
   219	`WorkspaceRead`; both would exceed the permitted boundary. It also avoids any
   220	claim that all overlay inputs are canonical: raw lookup behavior remains
   221	unchanged whenever entries exist and spelling can affect the answer.
   222	
   223	## Discriminating checks required before acceptance
   224	
   225	### Focused RED/GREEN checks
   226	
   227	1. **Empty overlay counter discriminator.** With
   228	   `ResolutionOverlaySnapshot::default()`, use the attribution-enabled counter
   229	   rail (or a test-only counter local to this private lookup), call `get` with a
   230	   deliberately noncanonical path, assert `None`, and assert zero normalizer
   231	   calls after the fix. Before the branch this must be RED with one call. Do not
   232	   expose a production counter API merely to write this test.
   233	2. **Nonempty raw-ingress control.** Construct one upsert using a canonical key,
   234	   query it with a backslash/`./` spelling that requires canonicalization, assert
   235	   the same `Some(source)` and exactly one lookup normalization. This prevents
   236	   widening the trust boundary to arbitrary lookup inputs.
   237	3. **Nonempty tombstone control.** The same raw/canonical spelling pair over a
   238	   tombstone must still produce `Some(None)` through the normalizing path.
   239	4. **Unknown noncanonical key control.** On a nonempty overlay, an absent raw key
   240	   must still be normalized before absence is concluded. This distinguishes the
   241	   empty-map proof from an unsafe “try raw then assume absent” shortcut.
   242	5. **Revert control.** Removing only the empty branch must restore one call in
   243	   check 1 while leaving checks 2-4 green.
   244

    82	## Reading
    83	
    84	The component-meta output digest oracle is equal on base and candidate (`7161214711717846280`); the
    85	compiled-output digest is UNOBSERVED by this cell (`evidence/A6/baseline-measurement.md:177`; the
    86	`compiled_output` determinism line reads `N/A (no observations)` in both TSVs), so no equivalence
    87	claim is made for compiled output. Every parse/build/admission `calls` counter is equal; the rows
    88	that differ are listed exhaustively in "Counters that differ" below. The candidate is **slower**: +12.35 % wall on a cold 40-component batch, driven by an **85 % increase in
    89	canonical-id normalizations** (9,656 extra calls, longer inputs — 20.7 vs 15.5 bytes per call) and
    90	+33 % allocations inside `session.semantic_dispatch` (see "Counters that differ" for the full set of
    91	rows that moved). The counter that exposes
    92	this is the one the crate move had silently dropped (`governance-join.md`, class 2 defect): had it
    93	not been restored, `workspace.normalize_canonical_id.calls` would read 0 and the `absolute_max` gate
    94	would PASS.
    95	
    96	Diagnosis (mechanism, for the adversarial-performance mandate to confirm): the relocated resolver's
    97	call sites are one-to-one with the deleted `ProjectResolver` (compare the `normalize_canonical_id`
    98	call lists in `identity-map.md`'s source and destination files), so the extra calls are not new
    99	sites — they are **re-executions**. The `ModuleResolverCore::resolve_attempt` kernel is a pure
   100	function of the `ResolverAttemptView`; the workspace driver (`verter_workspace/src/resolver.rs::
   101	drive_attempt`) re-runs the whole attempt after every `NeedInputs` wave, so the pure resolution
   102	prefix (`parent_dir`/`join_paths` → `collapse_path` → `normalize_canonical_id`, owner selection,
   103	`normalized_starts_with`) executes once per wave instead of once per resolution
   104	(`resolution_conversion_tests::full_driver_resolves_via_a_workspace_alias` asserts ≥ 3 waves for
   105	one alias resolution). The old engine resolved in a single pass with live reads. This is a property
   106	of the ratified `AttemptOutcome`/`NeedInputs` design as implemented (no prefetching frontier across
   107	waves, no per-attempt memo), not of any one edit — which is why it is reported here rather than
   108	patched: reducing waves or memoizing derived path values across waves is a production design change
   109	the landing-path ruling does not order ("no production rewrite is ordered"), and reweighting or
   110	reinterpreting the cell is forbidden (S2-F6).
